articleTitle: Space-time codes for active antenna systems: Comparative performance analysis
abstract: In this paper, the basic tools for performance analysis of space-time coding for active antenna systems (or colocated coherent MIMO systems) are presented, and illustrated with four different space-time codes: M-sequences, Alltop codes - quadratic and cubic -, and multiple shifted chirps. The relative effectiveness of these different codes is then measured with specific factors of merit, designed for radar performances evaluation. These factors of merit, easily extracted from the ambiguity functions, are shown to allow operational consequences to be drawn from space-time codes characteristics.

articleTitle: An improved scheme of Digital Beam-Forming in elevation for spaceborne SAR
abstract: In the high-resolution, wide-swath imaging application of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR), Digital Beam-Forming (DBF) technique can be employed to receive and handle echo data with multiple channels in elevation, for the purpose of increasing the receive gain and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). According to the geometric relationship among these channels, this paper analyzes the impulse response function of arbitrary elevation channel, and derives its explicit expression. Based upon this, an improved DBF processing scheme, which combines the time-variant weighting and Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filtering, is presented. Additionally, the block diagram of this DBF configuration is given. Compared with other echo-receiving methods, this approach can maximize the receive gain and optimize the system performance for the case of long pulse, without much increase of the system complexity. Simulation results indicate that it enables the system to achieve its theoretically optimal receiving performance.

articleTitle: A novel channel phase bias estimation method for spaceborne along-track multi-channel HRWS SAR in time-domain
abstract: Multi-channel Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) in azimuth, which can be utilized to suppress the Doppler ambiguity to achieve the High-Resolution Wide-Swath (HRWS) SAR images, suffers from the amplitude and phase mismatch among the channels. This paper presents a novel data-based phase bias estimation method in time-domain. Firstly, the echoes in time-domain received by the adjacent channels are processed to get interferometric phases, which consist of the Doppler centroid information and the difference of the phase biases between the adjacent channels. Then, the Doppler centroid can be extracted by circular integral of the adjacent interferometric phases. Finally, the phase bias between each channel and the reference one can be obtained by integral of the interferometric phase subtracted by the phase of the Doppler centroid. Using the presented method, both the phase bias and the Doppler centroid of the raw echoes can be effectively estimated. The performance of presented method is validated by the experiments of simulated spaceborne multi-channel SAR data.

articleTitle: Fast generation Of SAR deceptive jamming signal based on inverse Range Doppler algorithm
abstract: For deceptive jamming against Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), generating jamming signal of large scene is difficult, due to its huge computation. However, it is acceptable to generate jamming signal in real-time but in low precision. Based on inverse Range Doppler algorithm (IRDA), a realtime deceptive jamming method for large scene is proposed in this paper. An analysis of the degradation of jamming image caused by an approximation in the method is done. Simulation results verify the rationality of the approximation and the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Hycam: A new S band surface radar testbed
abstract: In 2008, ONERA started designing, for the French MoD, an S band surface radar testbed in the aim to support studies of new radar architectures. The core idea was to build a “high versatility system” able to collect data representative of most of ongoing radar projects, but also to prepare future developments. Within this context, we have defined and built a system that can address studies such as the use of new waveforms, multi function's scheduling optimisation, the benefit of using high bandwidths for recognition, the advantage of polarimetry for target or environment identification, beam sharpening, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) configurations, etc...The system, named HYCAM, was delivered late 2011 and this paper presents its main features and components.

articleTitle: Radar emitter signal recognition based on time-frequency analysis
abstract: The extraction of radar emitter identification is very important to distinct the correct target. Up to now, many corresponding methods are proposed. But most of it has the problems of low recognition rate and not adapting to low SNR environment. In the paper, a novel method is proposed. The approach utilizes time-frequency analysis methods and singular value distribution(SVD) to extract the singular values of signal, making it be the feature vector., and neural network based classifiers were designed to identify radar emitter signals automatically. The experimental results show that it can achieve a satisfying accurate recognition rate when signal-to-noise rate varies in a large range. It is proved to be valid and practical approach.

articleTitle: A method for extracting radar words of multi-function radar at data level
abstract: In syntactic modeling, radar words that are encoded into pulse sequences are basic for recognition of multi-function radar(MFR). To deal with the problem of extracting radar words from stream of pulse description word(PDW), an extracting method at data level is presented. Firstly, TTP(TOA to PRI) transform method, a pulse sequence analysis method, is improved and expanded. By combining TOA and the other parameters in PDW, multidimensional figure is obtained for joint identification of radar words. Simulation results show that the intuitive method can reduce the effect of drop pulses and false pulses, and extract the radar words of MFR availably.

articleTitle: Multisensor-multitarget tracking based on hierarchical association only using rangedoppler measurements
abstract: The azimuthal resolution of high frequency surface wave Radar (HFSWR) is usually coarse due to the difficulty to build a sufficiently huge antenna array. Effective solution to the problem of target locating and tracking with non-angular measurements is of significance. Once it is solved, the sensors, such as HFSWR, do not have to use antenna with large aperture size any more. Aiming at the existence of `Ghost point' in the ranging cross locating system this paper presents a hierarchical association algorithm. Based on the Range-Doppler observed by a single sensor, the nearest neighbour joint probability data association algorithm (NNJPDA) is adopted firstly to establish local track data, then the Ghost points are eliminated according to the target speeds measured by the two sensors respectively. The 0-1 integer programming is used to eliminate Ghost points further and provide the final association results. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Direct digital generation of ultra-wideband LFM signal and its compensation technology
abstract: The linear frequency modulated signal is widely used in radar systems, and two methods, which are DDS and DDWS, are mainly used to generate the baseband signal. This system adopts the DDWS method, based on FPGA parallel theory and high-speed DAC framework, to generate the broadband linear frequency signal with bandwidth of 500MHz. The principle of filter-based pre-distortion compensation presented in the paper is used for the amplitude and phase compensation of system, and the ration of the main lobe to the side lobe after pulse compression has a significant improvement. Detailed steps about the implementation are given in this paper.

Author Keywords: the compensation of amplitude and phase pre-distortion

articleTitle: Robust DOA estimation for a MIMO array using two calibrated transmit sensors
abstract: Traditional direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for a MIMO array assumes perfect knowledge of the array manifold. Its performance will degrade severely in the presence of array model errors. In this paper we propose a simple scheme for robust DOA estimation based on a MIMO array configuration, where two well-calibrated transmit sensors are used as the transmit array and no knowledge about the receive array manifold is assumed. Its performance is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of stepped frequency continuous wave Ground-Based SAR
abstract: GBSAR (Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar) is an effective supplement to Space-borne SAR and Air-borne SAR, as well as an experimental platform for deformation detection and verification of advanced microwave imaging modes and algorithms. This paper first introduces the basic principle and structure of SFCWGBSAR (Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave GBSAR) developed by IECAS (Institute of Electronics Chinese Academy of Sciences), followed by the analysis of imaging principle and performance of SFCW (Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave). Frequency sampling of SFCW utilizes IDFT to realize range compression without match filtering, which simplifies the imaging algorithm, lowers the sampling rate of AD converter and reduces the data size in imaging. A simulation of SFCW range compression is conducted and the result is consistent with the analysis of SFCW's imaging performance. Finally, an experiment is presented and the result verifies the imaging ability of SFCWGBSAR.

articleTitle: A novel imaging algorithm for circular scanning SAR based on the Cardano's formula
abstract: For circular scanning synthetic aperture radar(CSSAR) this new imaging modality, the curve moving trajectory makes the two-dimensional spectrum difficult to approach. This paper proposed a new imaging algorithm for the CSSAR based on derivation of the spectrum by the Cardano's formula. In the whole processing, only one quartic range approximation is adopted to ensure that the algorithm is precise enough to focus the image. At last, simulation results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Bandwidth synthesis for stepped chirp signal: A multichannel sampling prospective
abstract: A stepped chirp signal bandwidth synthesis algorithm is proposed based on the multichannel sampling theory. The sub-band signals are viewed as the responses of a group of linear time-invariant (LTI) filters with a wideband chirp signal as the common input. The reconstruction is formulated both in the time and frequency domain using the multichannel sampling theorem. Simulation results show that the proposed method is able to suppress the paired echoes and improve the integrated sidelobe ratio in the high resolution range profile.

articleTitle: A subbandadaptive filter for DTV based passive radar
abstract: In passive radar, the direct and multipath interference in echo channel must be suppressed before target detection. As the bandwidth of the digital television(DTV) signal is quite broad, when target detection is performed utilizing DTV signal, the inconsistency of the reference channel and the echo channel will leads to the degradation of the cancellation gain and radar operation range. To solve this problem, a novel interference suppression approach is proposed. First, the direct wave and the echo signals are decomposed into subbands and down-sampled; then in each subband, signal passes through a Wiener filter; last, the final output can be obtained by synthesizing the interpolated results of the subband filtering. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves the cancellation performance effectively.

articleTitle: Block NLMS cancellation algorithm and its real-time implementation for passive radar
abstract: The major interference in passive radars is the direct path and multipath clutter, which should be cancelled before matched filter processing generally. The block normalized least-mean-squares (block NLMS or BNLMS) algorithm, in which the weight vector is updated only once every occurrence based on a block gradient estimation, is exploited and implemented by using graphics processing unit (GPU) for real-time adaptive clutter cancellation. Validated by experimental data and theoretical analysis, the BNLMS algorithm can provide better performance in both cancelling capability and computation efficiency, which especially, is great for the wideband signal-based passive coherent location (PCL) radars owing to their strong noise and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of passive GNSS-based SAR imaging modes
abstract: This paper presents experimental methods and results obtained with passive bistatic SAR based on navigation satellites (e.g. GPS, GLONASS or Galileo) as transmitters of opportunity. Different imaging modes are considered. These include a stationary receiver, as well as a receiver onboard a ground moving vehicle and a real aircraft. The experimental setup in each case is described, and the corresponding imagery obtained is presented and discussed. The obtained results clearly demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed technology on the practical level.

articleTitle: Simulation of geosynchronous radar and atmospheric phase compensation constraints
abstract: Several concepts have now been published for geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR). The long distance means that to achieve a satisfactory signal to noise ratio, the signal integration time may be minutes or hours. Over this period the atmosphere cannot be assumed static and phase compensation for atmospheric perturbations is needed. A simulator has been developed to quantify the performance of candidate phase compensation schemes and thus to evaluate the conditions in which GEO SAR imaging is expected to be feasible. A process to design a GEO SAR system (low inclination) compatible with the atmospheric imaging constraints is presented, along with some candidate results.

articleTitle: Time and phase synchronization for wideband distributed coherent aperture radar
abstract: The distributed coherent aperture radar as a new radar technology is expected to be the next generation radar, which is much easier to transport and less expensive than traditional large aperture radar. However, the time synchronization and phase synchronization between unit radars are key issues to realize the full coherence for wideband distributed coherent aperture radar. Therefore, the time synchronization technique and the phase synchronization technique are investigated respectively in this paper. At first, the error sources of time synchronization and phase synchronization are analysed, and the corresponding mathematical models are developed. Then, the corresponding simulations are carried out to analyse the impact of synchronization error on the coherent performance. At last, the time synchronization and the phase synchronization schemes are proposed respectively based on the noncorrelation transmission technique and the calibration technique by utilizing the wired transmission. Research on the synchronization problem will be very helpful for realization of wideband distributed aperture coherent radar.

articleTitle: A research on SAR autofocusing algorithms for compressive sensing technique
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) theory, which is proposed in the recent years, has a significant effect on acquiring and transferring a super vast amount of data. The incoherent measurement in CS theory can solve the acquiring and transferring problem in high resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging effectively. The application of the CS theory in SAR autofocusing will induce important changes in the field of the radar technique. In this paper,the CS theory is applied into the SAR autofocusing. The implementation of the autofocusing method based on the CS theory is analyzed, the algorithms are proposed, the improvement measure aiming at the sparse signal is discussed. At last, field data experiment is proceeded to validate the performance of the algorithms and to compare the merits.

articleTitle: Research on mono-pulse forward-looking imaging airborne radar system
abstract: In radar system, by comparison of sum and difference signal for each echo received, mono-pulse technology implements accurate angle measurement. Within a two-dimension area in front of the airborne imaging radar, the detailed azimuth information can be acquired by antenna's continuous azimuth scanning, while the high resolution range information can be realized by pulse compression. Based on mono-pulse airborne radar system, a sort of forward-looking imaging algorithm is analyzed and a system working flow is proposed in the paper. It is verified by simulation and experiment that the proposed system can realize forward-looking imaging that in other ways, both Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Doppler Beam Sharpening (DBS) technology fail to. Besides, the imaging quality acquired is better than real beam imaging.

articleTitle: Adaptive mainlobe jamming suppression method for STAP airborne radar
abstract: In this paper, spatial adaptive mainlobe jamming suppression method for STAP airborne radar is proposed, utilizing sum, difference and auxiliary channels, which will dramatically degrade the implementation of airborne radar system. The method performs well when there are mainlobe and sidelobe jamming, and maintains excellent clutter suppression performance in conjunction with STAP. In this paper, the performance results obtained by measured data demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in jamming environment for STAP-based airborne radar, where only the spatial pattern forming is considered. Besides, the presented method is also applicable to continuous aperture radar.

articleTitle: GEO SAR interferometry: Theory and feasibility study
abstract: Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) is the satellite running on the 36,500-Km altitude orbit, and its period is almost 1-day. As we all know, if there is no effect of perturbation force, the orbit of the GEO SAR will coincident exactly per period, and there will be no baseline to achieve interferometry. However in practice, there are varieties of perturbation force in the space, so the orbit in different periods is no longer coincident, which makes it possible to achieve interferometry. In this paper, we study two typical GEO SAR orbits, and analyze the nadir-point trajectory excursion due to orbital perturbation using the software STK (Satellite Tool Kits, AGI). Based on the interferometry theory, we define the repeat-pass baseline of the GEO SAR, and obtain the height measurement accuracy of different kinds of orbits. At last, we verify the feasibility of GEO SAR interferometry by simulation.

articleTitle: Empirical performance analysis of Linear Frequency Modulated pulse and Multitones on UWB software defined radar prototype
abstract: In this study, we apply a protocol for an unbiased analysis of radar signals' performances. Using an experimental UWB software-defined radar, range profile, Doppler profile and detection range are evaluated for both Liner Frequency Modulated pulse and Multitones. The radar was prototyped and is comparable in overall performance to software defined radar test-beds found in the literature. The measured performances are in agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: A micro-motion measurement method based on wideband radar phase derived ranging
abstract: The value of micro-motion measurement has become increasingly prominent in the field of target detection and identification, and micro-motion extraction for target recognition demands radar's ability to get both high range resolution and high Doppler resolution. In this paper, we study on the technology of phase derived ranging (PDR) based on wideband radar. Its sub-millimeter ranging accuracy guarantees to extract target micro-motion features effectively, and on the other hand overcomes the shortcomings of the narrowband micro-Doppler separation technology, such as range glint and its failure to obtain the exact position of micro-motion over complex targets. A series of experiments verify the high-precision ranging capability of the wideband radar whose ranging accuracy can reach 0.1 mm, and the high phase stability of the wideband radar ensure feature measurement of very small amplitude fretting. This method can be applied to the target micro-motion feature inversion, and provides an effective approach for target recognition.

articleTitle: Analysis of horn antennas including the horn transition into half space employing a full wave hybrid technique
abstract: A technique combining mode-matching (MM) and method of moment (MoM) is presented for analysis of a stepped junction horn radiating into half space. 2-D MoM technique using Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) function has been applied for horn radiating into half space and MM has been applied for stepped junction. Studies have also been performed on choice of RWG function for this modeling. The codes have been implemented in Matlab to study the performance of this full wave hybrid technique for the case of a rectangular horn antenna. Computed results have been compared with simulation results obtained using HFSS-14 and close match is observed.

articleTitle: Radar assignment for stealth targets detection and tracking based on BPSO in air-defense radar network
abstract: In this paper we consider the radar assignment problem for air-defense radar network to detect and track multiple stealth targets. For the purpose of selecting appropriate radar at appropriate time to optimize the detection and tracking performance under the given constraints, we propose a novel radar assignment algorithm based on posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound (PCRLB), binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) and particle filtering (PF). A group of randomly generated particles are used to obtain the detection probability of newborn targets, while the tracking accuracy is measured by PCRLB. Moreover, the BPSO is adopted to search the surveillance region for the optimal activated radar subset. Finally, the PF outputs of activated radars are fused. Simulation results show that the proposed method can not only quickly identify newborn targets, but also can optimize the tracking performance of existing targets. Compared with traditional methods, the tracking accuracy of the radar network is improved.

articleTitle: Employing DGS structures in dual-band antennas for MIMO applications with high port isolation
abstract: This letter investigates the effect of mutual coupling on the operation of a dual-band MIMO antenna system. A rectangular codirectional split ring resonator-type (RCSRR) defected ground structure (DGS) is designed to isolate the antennas and reduce the influence of coupling on radiation characteristics. This compact dual-band DGS structure consists of two codirectional split rings resonator and locates between two patches, and the dimension of each ring controls the corresponding resonant frequency. Two multiantenna prototypes are fabricated and experimentally evaluated. Measurement results confirm the improvement of isolation between the antennas at the radiation frequency of 2.3/4 GHz when the DGS is utilized. The measured isolation of antenna with DGS has obviously improved than that of the original one in two operating bands. The predicted results agreed very well with measured data.

articleTitle: A novel omnidirectional microstrip coaxial collinear antenna array
abstract: In this paper, a kind of omnidirectional microstrip coaxial collinear (COCO) antenna array is designed, fabricated, and tested. The antenna is fabricated by standard printed circuit board technology (PCB), with overall dimension of 300×30×0.8mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The measured bandwidth of the antenna is about 4% with VSWR less than 1.4. The antenna has stably omnidirectional H-plane radiation patterns in the whole effective bandwidth, while the measured maximum gain reaches 4.85dBi at the highest frequency. Good agreement between the simulations and measurements is observed.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband multistatic tracking of human targets
abstract: Multistatic ultra-wideband radar is acknowledged to be useful for through-wall human tracking. In this paper, the global information processing chain for a multistatic ultra-wideband radar system is described, and experimental results are provided to validate the approach for Through-The-Wall detection and location of moving human targets. The design options for the system are first presented and justified, and the required information processing steps are briefly summarized. Special attention is then devoted to the issue of tracks association between different receivers, and an information-based technique exploiting range-Doppler video sequences from each receiver is shown to be an adequate solution. Finally, the overall structure of the information processing chain is summarized, and the remaining areas for research are outlined.

articleTitle: Circular SAR motion compensation using trilateration and phase correction
abstract: Circular SAR (CSAR) has raised an increasing interest in recent years. As a new SAR imaging mode, it has the ability to achieve sub-wavelength resolution for isotropic targets on planar ground and 3-D reconstruction<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. However the high resolution depends on high accuracy of platform position. For CSAR systems operating at centimeter wavelength, cm-level accuracy Position and Orientation Systems (POS) couldn't fulfill the requirements. Motion compensation is the key technique to obtain focused CSAR images. In this paper, we propose a method for CSAR motion compensation based on echo data which does not rely on high precision POS .It combines trilateration and phase correction. Calibrators are used to help reconstructing flight trajectory. The approach is validated via simulation.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler feature extraction using single-frequency radar for high-speed targets
abstract: The micro-motion of radar targets commonly mixes with bulk translation. In order to extract the micro-Doppler signature of moving targets during a long observation time, it is necessary to perform coherent preprocessing on the echo to compensate the bulk translation. This paper first derives the narrowband echo model for high-speed targets with precession and gives a coherent preprocessing algorithm based on the echo model. Then the micro-Doppler signature is analyzed by joint time frequency transform and the micro-motion period is estimated by a method based on inverse radon transform. Finally, the proposed algorithm is verified with the simulation echo of a cone with precession.

articleTitle: Design of spaceborne SAR imaging processing and fast Verification Based on FPGA
abstract: Realization of real-time processing for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) based on FPGA is a tough work because of its complicated algorithm, huge data and difficulty of debugging on board. This paper first analyses the characteristic of FPGA and puts forward fast pulse compression architecture. System-level simulation of FPGA software for spaceborne SAR is carried out by the new way of system verification techniques. According to the hardware environment, system-level simulation model is composed of system input and output, high speed memory interface and DSP interface. Fast debugging for spaceborne SAR imaging software is implemented and its validity has been verified.

articleTitle: Threshold setting of track-before-detect based on dynamic programming for radar target detection
abstract: The track-before-detect based on dynamic programming is a new non-coherent integrated technology. It tries to integrate the energy of a target along the path of the target moving in a lot of frames and finally makes a decision about the presence or absence of a target according to a preset threshold. The threshold is often difficult to be set appropriately. A new method for setting the threshold is presented in this paper. The method combines the theoretical computation with our experience. Results of the simulated experiments show that the DP-TBD with the proposed threshold works very well, which will lay the foundation for the practical application of the DP-TBD.

articleTitle: Comparison study of two approaches for bioradar data processing
abstract: In this paper, we present a feasibility study for life signs detection using a continuous wave radar working in the band around 4 GHz. The data processing is carried out by using two different data processing approaches, which are compared about the possibility to characterize the frequency behaviour of the breathing and heartbeat activity. The two approaches are used with the main aim to show the possibility to monitor the vital signs activity in an accurate and reliable way.

articleTitle: Synthetic aperture radar processing using a novel implementation of fast factorized back-projection
abstract: Due to the heavy computational complexity, the efficiency of FFBP algorithm descends obviously. Thus, an approximate FFBP algorithm is proposed in this paper. With the imaging plane on the r - sinθ coordinate system, there is no need to calculate the arcsines of the back-projected angle. Meanwhile, the polynomial estimation method is introduced to obtain the approximate values of back-projected slant range and angle. As a result, the number of operations is further reduced. A detailed analysis of computation burden is given as well. At the end of the paper, dealing with the data of different wavebands, the simulation result of the point targets shows that the algorithm proposed is accurately and effective to give well focused images.

articleTitle: Scan performance of low index lens reflector
abstract: A compact 26dBi gimballed lens reflector antenna was developed for aeronautical Q-band application. The design has a stationary feed and consequently does not require rotary joints. A 4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> radius hemispherical homogeneous low relative permittivity lens was shown through both simulation and experiment to meet the required gain specification across ±48° scan range, obviating the need for a Luneburg Lens as stated in most prior work. Consequently, the final antenna design had a minimum number of parts and could be conveniently manufactured using a numerically controlled milling machine. The measured scan performance of the different scalar feed - lens combinations agreed well with simulations of a spherical lens fed by those same feeds. The full wave spherical lens simulations were in general agreement with equivalent prior work done using empirical equations, despite some ripple in the focal length-gain curves.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wide swath SAR based on variable PRF and Digital Beamforming
abstract: To realize the ultra-wide swath SAR imaging with a fine resolution, which enables a shortened revisit time for frequent global mapping, an innovative multiple elevation beam (MEB) SAR based on variable PRF and Digital Beamforming (DBF) with the reflector antenna is proposed. Such a system employs DBF technique to effectively improve SNR and suppress the range ambiguities, and the use of deployable reflector antenna avoids the implementation complexity compared with the planar antenna. Furthermore, a novel strategy of linear variation of pulse repetition interval (PRI) is effectuated to overcome the blind-range problem of the conventional MEB SAR. The system configuration and imaging scheme are described in detail. A typical example spaceborne SAR based on the presented technique is designed. Simulation results denote that the presented SAR system shows satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: High resolution detection in application of railway radar system
abstract: To improve the safety of the railway system, the obstacle sensing radar system for railway is of great interest. High resolution radar can provide more information of the target, hence is suitable for the application in railway system. In this paper, we investigate the high resolution detection in railway radar. A double threshold generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) detector, which is robust over different scattering density, is proposed for the detection. The threshold selection strategy is also given to guarantee the constant false-alarm rate (CFAR). The proposed algorithm is verified by an experimental radar system whose bandwidth is 1GHz.

articleTitle: Optimal ISAR imaging time selection of ship targets using real data
abstract: The optimal imaging time selection of ship targets using Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) real data is investigated in this paper. The Doppler centroid frequencies (DCF) of a series of images obtained over continuous short durations are used to estimate the variations of the ship sway. The optimal imaging time including the optimal imaging instants and optimal imaging duration is determined by locating the maximum DCF and using the image contrast maximization criteria, respectively. Real data processing verifies the effectiveness of the proposed imaging method.

articleTitle: Development of distributed aperture coherence - synthetic radar technology
abstract: Based on SNR Gain, the distributed aperture coherence-synthetic radar(DACR) is derived by introducing the development of coherence - synthetic technology, and its working principle and some basic concepts are discussed, as well as the key technologies with solution way. At last, both domestic and overseas verification experiments of DACR are shown.

articleTitle: Automatic recognition of radar signals based on time-frequency image character
abstract: Radar signal recognition is one of the key technologies of modern electronic surveillance systems. Time-frequency image provides a new way for recognizing the radar signals. In this paper, a series of image processing methods containing image enhancement, image threshold binarization and mathematical morphology is utilized to extract the shape character of smoothed pseudo wigner-ville time-frequency distribution of radar signals, and then realize the identification of radar signals by the character. Simulation results of eight kinds of typical radar signals demonstrate that when signal noise ratio (SNR) is greater than -3dB, the Legendre moments shape character of the time-frequency image is very stable. Moreover, the recognition rate by the character is more than 90% except for the FRANK code signal when SNR ≥ -3dB. Compared with existing algorithms, the proposed algorithm also has advantages of less character dimension and shorter computation time.

articleTitle: Cross-range scaling combining motion compensation for ISAR imaging
abstract: The techniques of accurate cross-range scaling and motion compensation both play significant roles in inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. This paper proposes a new method to estimate motion parameters for ISAR targets scaling as well as motion compensation. With a time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) model, the pole histories of dominant scatters can be obtained. According to the time-frequency relationship, motion parameters including the effective rotational velocity and the coefficients of phase error are extracted. Using these parameters, we can not only scale the image but also compensate phase error to focus the image. Simulation and real-data experiments illustrate its feasibility and robustness.

articleTitle: Establishment and analysis of accurate signal model for forward-looking imaging radar with motion platform
abstract: In this paper, the effect of platform movement on the echo signal of forward-looking imaging radar is studied through establishing accurate echo signal model. Based on the geometric relationships between platform movement and beam scanning, the mathematical expressions of instantaneous scanning velocity, the illumination starting time and lasting time are derived. Through analyzing the accurate echo signal model, it is found that platform movement causes imaging target's deviation from the actual location and pattern distortion. At last, simulations demonstrating this effect are carried out. This paper provides theoretic basis for forward-looking radar imaging data processing.

Author Keywords: illumination starting time and lasting time

articleTitle: Noise jamming to ISAR based on multiplication modulation
abstract: Based on multiplication modulate method, this paper analyses the noise jamming to ISAR. The noise jamming signal of traditional method has no correlation with ISAR radar signal, and is easily dismissed. So, in this paper the imaging principle of inverse synthetic aperture radar is analyzed, the noise jamming method based on multiplication modulates against ISAR are discussed, and the correlation between jamming signal and radar signal is presented. Simulation proves the correctness of the presented analysis and proposed noise jamming method.

articleTitle: A novel particle filtering algorithm based on state fusion
abstract: To address the limitations of the particle filter algorithm (PF), we propose the fusioned particle filter (FPF). In this new method, the importance density function is generated by state fusion of the extended Kalman filter algorithm (EKF) and the unscented Kalman filter algorithm (UKF). To construct the importance density of samples, the state of each particle is predicted according to the EKF and the UKF, successively. And the feedback of state estimation from the last step is used to implement the update of particles. Thus, using the most of recent measurements and the additional feekback information, FPF can obtain an accurate approximation to the nonlinear non-Gaussian system and as a result, improve the estimation performance. An application example is given to draw a comparison between the FPF and the existing particle filter algorithms. The simulation results show the efficiency of this new approach.

articleTitle: The performance analysis of micro-Doppler extracted from radar echoes under different bandwidth
abstract: Sideband Doppler modulation caused by micro motion of targets on radar echoes is called micro-Doppler effect. Vibration, swing, rotation, coning, precession and nutation are the most common kinds of micro motion. In this paper, micro-Doppler is induced by coning motion mathematically. Then echoes of point scatterers are modelled with linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal. This paper mainly studies the performance of micro-Doppler extracted from echoes of targets with translation compensated completely under different bandwidth. It is more beneficial to extract micro-Doppler characteristics of each scatterer respectively as the bandwidth grows wider, when different scatterers can be separated in range profile domain. At last, the analysis of performance is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A new method of multi-target detection for FMCW automotive radar
abstract: In multi-target situations, typically triangular FMCW radar brings out false targets and degrades the radar performance. A novel transmitted waveform and multi-target detection algorithm for automotive applications is presented in this paper. The proposed waveform is composed of three segments: up ramp, flat frequency and down ramp in every small period. Especially, the flat frequencies are modulated by a unique PN code sequence within a determinate frequency range. The unambiguous relative velocities detected in the flat frequency segment can cancel some false targets initially. Corresponding to the waveform, which combines the advantages of both FSK and FMCW formats, a progressive judgment algorithm is used in the continuous small period to further eliminate the false targets.

articleTitle: New parameters in compact polarimetry for ocean target detection
abstract: In this paper, we develop three new parameters for compact polarimetry to a particular application in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) maritime surveillance, i.e., the joint oil-spill and ship detection. Based on the X-Bragg rough surface scattering model, we investigate the capability of compact polarimetry, a dual-polarized system, for sea surface scattering characterization, and find that the circular-transmit-and-linear-receive (CTLR) mode has a better potential for sea surface representation. Then three parameters are used to discriminate the target scattering properties at sea. These parameters allow distinguishing oil spills from two kinds of look-a-likes, i.e., biogenic slicks and low-wind areas, and show good performance for ship detection. In addition, by investigating the relationship between the elements in CTLR mode and full-polarized mode, it is shown that in the simple scenario of sea surfaces, the three parameters have their approximations in the full-pol mode. The mutual related parameters (i.e., the proposed parameters in the CTLR mode and the corresponding approximations in the FP mode) have SAR signatures very similar to each other. At last, several polarimetric data sets, including Radarsat-2 C-band data, UAVSAR L-band data and SIR-C/X-SAR C-band data are studied for verification and demonstration.

articleTitle: An evaluation system for SAR real-time processing system
abstract: Real-time processing system is a very important part in the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system. It is necessary to assess the performance of a SAR real-time processing system comprehensively. An evaluation system is analyzed in this paper by classifying a real-time processing system into 3 types: single-node structure, serial structure and parallel structure. Several performance parameters are defined to assess the system performance, 4 parameters for processing unit: execution time, processing throughput ratio, speedup ratio and processor efficiency; 4 for processing system: number of processors, number of processing units, average processor load and standard deviation of the processor load. Based on a practical SAR real-time processing system, it is demonstrated that this evaluation system can comprehensively evaluate and effectively optimize the design of SAR real-time processing systems.

articleTitle: Multi-target frequencies and directions estimation algorithm for monobit digital wideband array receiver
abstract: A novel multiple target frequency and direction estimation algorithm, based on the single snapshot in frequency domain, is presented in this paper for the monobit digital wideband array receiver. For the optimal array model, the radio frequency array signal is sampled only one bit, i.e. the monobit digital wideband array receiver. By doing with the given monobit digital data, the frequency values and direction angles of the multiple targets can be obtained by the presented algorithm. The performances of multiple signal detection capability, such as independence, correlation and coherent targets, are analyzed by computer simulations. As a result, the simulation shows that the proposed algorithm is feasible, efficient and less sensitive to the random amplitude and phase errors.

articleTitle: An implantable stripline-fed slot antenna for biomedical applications
abstract: In this paper, a stripline-fed slot antenna for implanted devices is proposed. The antenna is characterized for the Industrial, Scientific and Medical Radio (ISM) band and applied to be implanted in muscle layer of the human body. Double-layered structure with slot both on top and bottom side of the antenna is used. The stripline-feed prevents the loss along the feed line regarding the in-body application and allows very high radiation efficiency. A miniaturization technology is applied by using a meandered line for the radiator connected with the stripline. The simulation and measured results show that the antenna with a small size of 12.5×14.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> features very good impedance matching in operational frequency band and a relative bandwidth of 16.9%, which indicates a high potential of this antenna for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Enhancement imaging on multi-path signals in ultra-wideband radar
abstract: This paper develops a method for enhancement imaging of objects when there are reflecting planes around in the environment. When the location of these planes is known, we can exploit the multipath signals reflected by them in imaging process. Coherent imaging algorithm, like backprojection (BP) algorithm, is typically achieved by direct returns. In this paper, a modified backprojection (MBP) coherent imaging algorithm is proposed to improve the image quality of interested targets by exploiting the multipath signals. The wave reflection analysis shows that, in order to obtain optimum resolution, the multipath signals should be processed before being used to imaging. The key points lie on the compensation of phase mutation and amplitude attenuation. After this process, the resolution of targets has a significant improvement. Simulations are used to validate the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Design of a novel DRFM jamming system based on AFB-SFB
abstract: In research of Electronic Countermeasure (ECM) recently, Jamming source based on Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) technology and digital channelization technology has attracted more attention. This paper schemes out a novel DRFM jamming system structure, which implementing the channelized receiving with Analysis Filter Bank (AFB) and the modulated signal reconstruction with Synthesis Filter Bank (SFB). Jamming information modulation is carried out in an optimized way with improved Signal Noise Ratio (SNR) of the generated signal. Simulation results have verified the validity of this scheme. Keywords: Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM), Analysis Filter Bank (AFB), Synthesis Filter Bank (SFB), deceptive jamming.

articleTitle: Multiple sources DOA and polarization estimations using vector circular array
abstract: This paper proposes a vector circular array with elements of uniform amplitude but different orientations for DOA and polarization estimations of source signals with relatively high grazing angles and arbitrary linear polarizations. It has advantages over conventional uniform circular array. Simulation results are shown to verify the performance of the proposed vector circular array.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of scanning mode in squinted SAR
abstract: The design of scanning mode is of significant meaning for synthetic aperture radars (SAR). Compared with conventional mechanical scanning, the two-dimensional non-uniform scanning mode based on the electronic control to obtain wide swath and uniform resolution is studied in this paper. Thus, it can the attitude disturbance of the radar platform more effectively. The procedure of electronic scanning mode is devised under the limits of attitude, resolution, swath and so on. In addition, the resolution characteristic of the system is analyzed under the scanning condition for the squinted SAR. A series of simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of this scanning method.

articleTitle: An efficient method to correct target range migration
abstract: In weak target detection, migration through range cells (MTRCs) of the moving targets with high velocities would affect the performance of long time coherent accumulation. To eliminate this effect, we may correct the MTRCs corresponding to the Doppler unambiguous part and ambiguous part respectively. Based on this thought, an improved algorithm is proposed in this paper, which gets the ambiguity numbers of multiple targets and corrects their MTRCs effectively. Then the energy of targets can be accumulated coherently in the end. Performance of simulations verifies the value of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection of range spread target with coherent integration
abstract: In this paper, a new detection method for range spread target with coherent integration is proposed. In this method, the Keystone transform is first applied to correct range migration of the target. Then coherent integration is employed to accomplish integration in time domain. Finally, range spread target detection is conducted in the Range-Doppler domain. The proposed detection method is generalized from current range spread target detectors such as the integrator, the SSDGLRT detector and the GLRT-DT detector. It can dramatically increase the detection signal-noise ratio (SNR) of those detectors and improve their detection performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic programming algorithm for the detection of air dim target
abstract: “Track-before-detection” (TBD) is well suitable for radar detection of dim targets because it takes advantage of the gains of time integration. Dynamic programming algorithm (DPA) is one of the traditional TBD techniques, and has been applied to sea dim target detection. In this paper, the expression of DPA applied to air dim target detection is given firstly. Important differences between air dim target and sea dim target is introduced in the application of DPA. In the end, numerical simulations show that air dim target detection based on DPA is limited in radar performance enhancement.

articleTitle: Log-periodic slot antenna with modified cavity
abstract: A cavity-backed log-periodic slot antenna which operates in 1-4.5GHz is presented. The antenna is fed by a special coplanar waveguide(CPW) that is gradual-changed and ultrawideband matched. Normal cavity is a high-Q resonator and will break the resonance of the antenna, especially at lower frequencies. A novel design of the cavity here is proposed to yield desired VSWR characteristics which is below 2.5 through the whole operation frequency band. The radiation patterns are unidirectional and quite stable within the band, which makes the antenna suitable for the applications in guidance, detection and UWB radar.

articleTitle: Phased array radar beamforming method based on MIMO radar covariance
abstract: A multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar is an emerging field which has attracted many researchers recently. In this type of radar, unlike an standard phased array radar, one can choose transmitted probing signals freely to maximize the power around the locations of the targets of interest, or more generally to approximate a given transmit beam-pattern, or to minimize the cross-correlation of the signals reflected back to the radar by the targets of interest. These signals can be correlated to each other or noncorrelated. Many papers have investigated beampattern design and waveforming in MIMO radars. One of the most famous approaches for beampattern design is named covariance based method which design cross-correlation matrix of transmitted signals instead of the signals. On the other hand, many papers have investigated beamforming of an standard phased array radar in different ways. In this paper it is desirable to design beampattern of a phased array radar by means of the MIMO radar covariance based beampattern design method, as a special case of general MIMO radar. Although many approaches are available for beamforming of phased array radar this approach would have less complexity compare to them. MATLAB software is being employed for simulations.

articleTitle: Experimental study using natural frequencies for fruit identification
abstract: This paper presents the experimental study for characterization of the ripening state of a fruit. The identification can be performed by comparing the libraries of natural poles, which can be extracted from its scattering response of the fruit. This experiment measures scattering responses from composite dielectric objects, and then applies the Cauchy method to extract the poles from the responses. Libraries of poles are catalogued to validate the identification system.

articleTitle: A novel design of parallel and high-speed signal processor architecture for PD radar
abstract: In this paper, a kind of high speed and parallel hardware architecture is designed with one TMS320C6678 and one XC6VSX315T. This system is used for the pulsed Doppler radar. To map the algorithm effectively, pipeline optimization on system and instruction levels are adopted, and various factors are taken into consideration, such as system complexity, communication between the processors, bandwidth of output signal.

articleTitle: A modified multiple hypothesis tracking algorithm with application to range and Doppler measurements
abstract: Multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) based on multiple scanning periods is theoretically the best method to solve data association problem. With the increasing target number and noise, the time spent on data association process will grow exponentially. To overcome the problem, a new modified MHT algorithm, which minimizes meaningless calculation, is proposed in this paper. The modified algorithm can make the data association process run faster by using a new method of establishing the data association tree. The modified algorithm is applied to range and Doppler measurement, and a comparison of the modified algorithm with traditional algorithm by computer simulation shows that the modified algorithm can decrease the runtime effectively when they have the same tracking performance.

articleTitle: Spurious components introduced by nonlinearity in Direct Digital Synthesis
abstract: In this paper, the mechanism of introducing spurious components by nonlinearity in Direct Digital Synthesisers (DDS) is analysed. An S-band frequency synthesiser for a stepped-frequency radar is presented. This frequency synthesiser is based on a DDS-driven wideband PLL architecture, which can achieve low spurious noise and rapid frequency hopping simultaneously. A novel DDS frequency planning method is utilised to ensure low colored noise within the entire output bandwidth. Measured results demonstrate that the overall SFDR is better than 58 dBc in a 320 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Effect of satellite attitude errors on spotlight SAR image
abstract: The spotlight SAR usually can realize a high resolution image, which needs the beam having the capability of beam scanning. The satellite attitude swing is a way to realize the beam scanning, but this way will cause the attitude jitter, then the image quality of spotlight SAR will be affected. So the effect of satellite attitude error on spotlight SAR is analyzed in this paper. First the paired echo is analyzed, which is caused by the error of satellite attitude, then the effect of attitude jitter on space-borne SAR image qualities is summarized based on the theoretical analysis and computer simulation. The analytical mathematical expression is deduced, which is useful in analysis of attitude stability and SAR image qualities. Moreover, the swing of the satellite antenna phase center is analyzed, and the effect on peak side-lobe ratio and integrated side-lobe ratio is shown. The computer simulations verify the effect of attitude errors on image quality.

articleTitle: Microwave staring imaging based on Bjorck-Schmidt orthogonlization
abstract: A new approach is proposed in this paper for microwave staring imaging. The time width and band width of the random signal is limited, so the correlation of the random radiation field is strong. By using the Bjorck-Schmidt orthogonlization algorithm, the non-correlation of the random radiation field is improved. Then, the correlation processing on the echo signal and the random radiation field is carried out and then higher quality staring image is obtained. The validation of the developed method is verified by the simulation.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing radar imaging under low SINR via waveform optimization
abstract: To enhance the performance of compressive sensing radar (CSR) imaging in low SINR, a waveform optimization method at the transmitter, instead of processing signal at the receiver, is proposed. The method can effectively improve the CSR range-Doppler imaging quality and reduce the target range-Doppler parameter estimation error in low SINR. Simulation results show the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Colocated MIMO radar sidelobe suppression using random space-time coding
abstract: For colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar transmitting orthogonal polyphase coded waveform, a low range, angular and Doppler sidelobe is desirable. In this paper, we propose a MIMO radar sidelobe suppression method based on random space-time coding (STC) method. In detail, at each pulse repetition period, a random STC matrix, composed of a diagonal random phase matrix multiplied by a random permutation matrix, is modulated to waveforms before transmission. Such a kind of STC matrix can keep the constant modulus property of transmitting waveforms and can decrease range, angular and Doppler sidelobe significantly.

articleTitle: An approach of bridge detection over water in high resolution SAR image
abstract: A new method to detect bridge over water in high resolution SAR images is presented. Firstly, 2-dimensional fuzzy feature is utilized to segment water regions in SAR image. Secondly, tree and hill shadow false targets are excluded based on 8-neighbour chain-code tracking edge method. Then the edge points of potential bridge ROIs (regions of interest) obtained by searching the water area are used to line fitting. In order to avoid the effect of stripe jamming, the fitted line segments are extended to gain the suspected bridge ROIs. Finally, the suspected bridge ROIs are segmented further by double parameter CFAR, and the bridges are detected by the principle axis direction and perimeter extracted. Experimental results show the algorithm can detect the bridges over water accurately, especially the bridges with subtle grey gradient variance or disturbed by stripe jamming in high resolution SAR image.

articleTitle: Design of dual-polarization and parallel-series-fed microstrip antenna array
abstract: A novel linear antenna array, combined dual-polarization with parallel-series-fed,is introduced in this paper. The type of the antenna is slot-coupled microstrip patch. Antenna consists of twenty microstrip patches. Antenna is designed in the frequency ranges about Ku-bands. The antenna array is series-fed so it is very easy to fabricate and quite low lost. The theoretical of return loss, isolation, and radiation patterns are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: SAR echo simulation from numerous scattering cells based on GPU
abstract: A comprehensive and novel SAR echo simulation method for a great deal of scattering cells is presented in this paper. In order to greatly reduce the processing time, we apply the Graphics Processing Units (GPU). Modern GPUs are very efficient at manipulating computer graphics, and their highly parallel structure makes them more effective than general-purpose CPUs in processing large blocks of data. Especially when facing the complicated scene of many scattering cells, high-speed operation in parallel based on GPU is perfectly fit. Via Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA), each thread of GPU is in charge of a single scattering cell, and thus this structure will highly improve the efficiency of echo simulation in complex scene.

articleTitle: Radar waveform design under the constraint of auto-correlation, orthogonality and Doppler tolerance
abstract: In order to improve the measurement capacity of fullpolarization radars, and take advantage of the target polarization information effectively, it is necessary to design suitable transmitting waveform to meet the requirement of full-polarization measurement. In this paper, a novel waveform design method is proposed. Greedy algorithm is used to optimize the phase-coded waveform design. The factors relative to auto-correlation and orthogonality performance are combined with the factor of Doppler tolerance in the cost function, and different phase-modulated waveforms could be designed to meet different requirement by adjusting their weights. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of this method.

articleTitle: L-band high efficiency GaN HEMT power amplifier for space application
abstract: This paper describes a high efficiency and high output power GaN power amplifier for L-band space application. The power amplifier module was developed using GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) device technology. The Matching Circuits were designed With a large-signal model developed by Cree. The special R-C parallel networks and gate resistance are used for cancellation of self-oscillation of low frequency and radio frequency at input matching circuit and bias circuits. The output impedance of a transistor under high power operation can be obtained by simulated load-pull results, which can be modeled by a parallel circuit of R and C. In the matching Circuit design, step-step impedance transformation matching technology is employed. Under Vds=28V, Vgs=-2.8V, 58W power amplifier achieves a 68% PAE at 1.19GHz under CW operating conditions.

articleTitle: RFI suppression algorithm based on median filter for SAR data
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method based on median filter for radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression applied to synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The RFI has higher power than the useful echo signal and has narrow property in range frequency domain. A threshold called max-mean-ratio (MMR) is proposed to detect the RFI existence. If the RFI exists, then the echo signal is processed with a median filter. The method is verified with the linear frequency modulation (LFM) and point target simulation. In the end, the method is applied to RadarSat-1 data to demonstrate the performance.

articleTitle: Tracking in the presence of RGPO or VGPO using the Kalman filter with a new modified PDA
abstract: The range gate pull off (RGPO) and the velocity gate pull off (VGPO) are two kinds of common electronic countermeasure techniques used to defeat or degrade tracking radars. For countering the RGPO or VGPO, the extended Kalman filter (EKF) with a new modified probabilistic data association (PDA) is proposed in this paper. It takes full advantage of the fact that for the case of low measurement noise, the measurements for the RGPO/VGPO have virtually the same Doppler velocity/range as those of the true target. This method uses the difference between the Doppler velocity and tracking velocity of the Kalman filter to weight the probability of every measurement so that less weight is given to the false measurement. The simulations show that for the case of low measurement noise, the EKF method with the new modified PDA can counter the RGPO or VGPO, and works better than the EKF with the standard PDA.

articleTitle: Impacts of wind turbine siting on radar clutter mitigation
abstract: As wind energy develops quickly, more commercial-scale wind turbines with high tower and large rotor diameter are emerging. These large man-made structures present interference to nearby radars in the form of radar clutter. This newly recognized type of clutter has unique radar signatures, making it difficult to be identified and mitigated. Based on analysing the characteristics of radar signatures, this paper suggests several wind turbine siting considerations solely from the perspective of radar clutter mitigation.

articleTitle: A full-aperture imaging algorithm for hybrid sliding spotlight bistatic SAR
abstract: A new full-aperture imaging algorithm for Spaceborne/ Airborne hybrid sliding spotlight bistatic SAR is proposed in this paper. The SAR configuration under discussion has great advantage over traditional ones, yet suffers from the double square-root term in the bistatic slant range equation and severe spatial variance. The proposed method firstly eliminates azimuth spectrum folding by the SPECAN operation, and then corrects the RCM by Chirp Scaling Algorithm. Without interpolation and sub-aperture operations, the algorithm is high in the computational efficiency and simple in the flow. Simulation results confirm the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Holographic subsurface imaging radar for applications in civil engineering
abstract: There is increasing demand in civil engineering to get high resolution images of shallowly buried objects such as steel reinforcements, power and communication lines, pipes, etc. The described in the article radar system employing continuous wave signals was designed to obtain plan view high resolution images at shallow depths. The plan view resolution is achieved by synthetic aperture, which is formed by regular manual scanning. The current design of the system has depth resolution defined by depth of focus rather than by bandwidth. Two narrowband prototypes of the system around 7 and 14 GHz were designed. The estimated resolution of the system in the presented experiments was estimated 2 and 1.5 cm at 7 and 14 GHz respectively. The paper outlines hardware, user and embedded software, hologram reconstruction technique, and selected experimental results.

articleTitle: A study on compensation of aperture fill time based on frequency-shifting
abstract: In consideration of aperture fill time caused by wide angle beam scanning, a novel algorithm based on frequency shifting is proposed for compensating aperture fill time, comparing with the conventional phase shifting method, which can only realize the synchronization of carrier phase, the proposed method can further realize the synchronization of modulated pulse phase, which can resolved coherent integration of modulated pulsed received by antenna array. The realization structure of frequency shifting method is given in theory from two processes of transmitting and receiving respectively, the range compensation is studied with emphasis, and the factors affecting range compensation accuracy are given. The simulation based on signal indicates the validity of modulated pulse phase synchronization by frequency shifting, and the relationship between SNR loss and range compensation accuracy is given in graph.

articleTitle: Signal integrity of high-performance and real-time signal processing system
abstract: As more and more new types and algorithms of radar system are exploited, higher-performance and real-time systems for signal processing have become inevitable. On this condition, signal integrity (SI) has become a significant issue which should be carefully considered by designers. In this paper, we presented a high-performance and real-time signal processing system designed for kinds of radars, and focused on three significant techniques suffering from signal integrity problems. We investigated the principles of them, and proposed some impactful rules and methods to improve the signal integrity of the system. The rules and methods can be used as reference to other congener signal processing systems. Additionally, hewing to the rules and methods, the system is working efficiently and stably.

articleTitle: A novel high-resolution imaging method for ROSAR
abstract: To improve the azimuth resolution performance which depends on the reconstruction angle in rotating synthetic aperture radar (ROSAR) system, a novel curved orbit approximation method based on the resampling and rotation of the transmitted and received pulse position is proposed. The approximation errors are calculated via an extended Taylor expansion and are compensated in the raw data domain. Precise two-dimensional (2-D) spectrum is derived and high resolution image is formed using extended omega-K algorithm for large scene. Feasibility and resolution performance of the proposed method are validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Time-shared fitting method of Doppler parameters and the implementation on FPGA
abstract: An essential part of SAR processing is the fitting of Doppler parameters, including the Doppler centroid frequency and the Doppler frequency rate. The traditional least squares fitting method is not practically used due to its heavy calculation burden. In this paper, we propose an improved time-shared fitting method of the Doppler parameters, which can reduce the resources and the time delay. The Doppler centroid frequency and the Doppler frequency rate need linear and quadratic fitting respectively. In this paper, only linear and quadratic fitting methods are discussed. Then the paper presents the implementation of the time-shared fitting method on FPGA. At last, the author analyzes the resources and time delay of the time-shared fitting method, and compares them with other fitting methods. The time-shared fitting method can save a lot of hardware resources and can reduce the time delay.

articleTitle: Design of frequency-scanning asymmetric antipodal Vivaldi antenna
abstract: An asymmetric antipodal Vivaldi antenna with frequency scanning function is proposed. The frequency scanning is achieved by two different exponential curves on the upper and bottom surfaces of the tapered slot antenna (TSA). The antenna is fed by microstrip line of 50 Ohm characteristic impedance. The proposed antenna shows 20.7% bandwidth from 6.5 GHz to 8.0 GHz with VSWR less than 2. The gain of the proposed antenna ranges from 5.4 dB to 6.75 dB through the whole effective bandwidth. The main beam of the E-plane radiation patterns at 6.5 GHz, 7.25 GHz, and 8 GHz, are 45 Deg, 50 Deg, and 60 Deg, respectively, which clearly displays the frequency scanning function of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Repeat jamming against LFM radars based on spectrum-divided
abstract: The paper presents a novel repeat jamming method capable of generating false targets in range from intercepted radar chirp signals. The proposed approach divides a received radar signal into several equal parts and then transmitted them back to the radar in a different order. The essence of the spectrum-divided jamming is that the spectrum of a radar chirp signal is separated into several equal pulses and rearranged in a different order to form a whole jamming signal before being retransmitted. The output of each jamming pulse after the matched filter is addressed. The divided number and the optimal retransmitted order are analyzed. Numeric simulations are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An autofocusing approach for airborne/stationary bistatic SAR imagery based on acquired raw data
abstract: An autofocusing approach for airborne/stationary bistatic synthetic aperture radar (A/S BiSAR) imaging was proposed in this paper. In A/S-BiSAR, not only the motion induced phase error but also the inaccuracy of data acquisition geometry (DAG) would seriously degrade the quality of the image in focus. In the proposed method, both the motion error and the influence of the inaccuracy of DAG were considered, and the introduced phase error was estimated and compensated. Well focused results from the acquired raw data were obtained and analyzed which validates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Coherent Radon transform based weak target detection for phased array radar
abstract: Range walk of the fourth generation fighters echo for traditional radar signal processing is a serious problem in the long coherent integration time. To solve the problem, a novel coherent Radon transform based weak target detection algorithm for metric-band phased array radar is proposed. First the echo signal model of supersonic weak target is provided, and the characteristic of range walk is analyzed. Based on this, the coherent Radon transform based long term coherent integration algorithm along the range walk line is presented. Finally, the performance of target detection and parameter estimation of the algorithm are analyzed by the simulation experiments, which suggest that the proposed algorithm has better detection performance compared with Hough transform method and MTD method.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of SSAP for clutter rejection in CP-OFDM signal based passive radar
abstract: Clutter rejection is a key technique in passive radar. Although many techniques have been implemented to solve this problem, it still presents great challenges due to the involved huge computational cost, the performance sensitivity to the extra environmental factors and so on. This paper investigates a novel subcarrier-based spatial adaptive processing (SSAP) which is tailored for the OFDM (orthogonal frequency division multiplex) modulation with a cyclic prefix (CP-OFDM). The algorithm principle is first illustrated and followed by the discussion about its advantages. Then the robustness is researched via evaluating the performance under relaxed basic assumptions. The conclusions are demonstrated by conducting on simulated and real data sets.

articleTitle: Modified sub-integer range alignment based on minimum entropy for ISAR
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) has the excellent capacity of generating image of noncooperative target. However, ISAR images are usually degraded due to relative motion between radar and target. In order to improve image quality, motion compensation is indispensable, and range alignment is just the first and key step of translational motion compensation. This paper proposes a sub-integer range alignment method based on minimum entropy, which has high accuracy of range alignment. The simulations are used to test the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Marine radar antenna height design under multi-path effect
abstract: The electromagnetic reflection from peaceful water surface causes multi-path effect, which will make the marine radar suffer from a blind zone of detection at some ranges. In this paper the relationship between the antenna vertical height and the detection blind zone is analysed. Moreover, in accordance with the scenario of installing multiple marine radars on one ship, a design principle for the vertical heights of multiple radar antennas is proposed, which reduces the blind zone coverage with the optimized combination of different vertical heights.

articleTitle: Wall parameter estimation using propagation time delay
abstract: Knowledge of the vital characteristics of the wall is particularly important for precise localization of targets across the wall in the through-wall imaging. A wall parameter estimation scheme based on the transmitted wave at a standoff distance (and the echo signal model) through the wall to the target is proposed. The mathematical model for target detecting through the wall body is derived. The derived transcendental equations (which consequence of the refraction interference by the wall body) are solved numerically. By comparing the numerical results with the measured results, wall parameters (thickness and permittivity) are estimated (which are closer to the actual measured situation).

articleTitle: A recursive algorithm for the design of array antenna in STAP application
abstract: As an effective reduced-dimension space time adaptive processing (STAP) approach, subarray technique is widely used in practice. However, it is hard to determine how many subarrays are necessary and what shape should they have. In this paper, a generalized form of STAP processing for arbitrary array is established. Then the subarray technique for STAP is discussed. In order to determine the optimum subarray partition, a recursive algorithm is proposed. Numerical results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: IPIX radar small target detection in sea clutter based on local backscattering amplitude statistics
abstract: A new method for small target detection in sea clutter is proposed. This approach builds on the local backscattering amplitude statistics of IPIX radar datasets: calculating the maxima and standard deviation (STD) of backscattering amplitude of different range bins. It is found that the maximum amplitude of the range bin hosting a small target (RBHST) is much smaller than that of other range bins hosting only sea clutter (ORBHSC) especially for the HH polarization datasets, the STD of RBHST is obviously larger than that of ORBHSC, upon this point, the small target within sea clutter can be detected accurately with no prior knowledge of ocean conditions.

articleTitle: Study on ground based space surveillance collocated MIMO radar
abstract: We introduce ground based collocated multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar with high angular and Doppler resolution capabilities into space surveillance. A new beam former is put forward to form fan shaped beam which will be useful to capture space targets with high resolution. Detection performance and beam characteristics are taken into account to determine the number of MIMO transmit elements. Theoretic analysis and simulation results both verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: System design and analysis of L-band aperture synthesis microwave radiometer
abstract: With three years of painstaking efforts, Xi'an Institute of Space Radio Technology has developed the Prototype of L-band Aperture Synthesis Microwave Radiometer (PLASMR). In this experiment, a large physical observation aperture by a thinned array of single small-aperture antennas has been designed to avoid the large size and weight of large-aperture antennas, to obtain high space resolution, and more importantly to better serve the satellite application and to observe and measure the sea salinity and soil moisture. Firstly, the paper presents the system design method and the structure of the Prototype of L-band Aperture Synthesis Microwave Radiometer (PLASMR). Secondly, the verification experiment was introduced. Lastly, the result of the nature target imaging is given. The development of the Prototype of L-band Aperture Synthesis Microwave Radiometer establishes engineering application for measuring the sea salinity and soil moisture.

articleTitle: Processing of SAR data based on the heterogeneous architecture of GPU and CPU
abstract: SAR imaging process is usually computationally burdensome and it is difficult to achieve SAR image in real-time. Recently, the rapid increase in the performance of Graphics Processing Units (GPU), coupled with powerful CPU, has made heterogeneous framework of GPU and CPU into a compelling platform for computationally demanding tasks. This paper presents the parallel implementation on the heterogeneous architecture using Chirp Scaling algorithm. Experimental results suggest that real-time imaging processing is possible for large-scale SAR data.

articleTitle: GB-SAR deformation monitoring: Performance analysis and primary experimental results
abstract: Ground-based synthetic aperture radar differential interferometer (GB D-InSAR) has already been recognized as a powerful tool, complementary to spaceborne SAR interferometry, for deformation monitoring. This application calls for rigid demand in measurement accuracy (to the degree of millimetre or even submillimeter). SAR trajectory error is one of the main factors degrading the measurement accuracy, and should be carefully considered.
