abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-layer half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) in-phase power combiner using a composite structure of multi-layer SIW B-plane branch and HMSIW T-junction. In order to balance the phase between output ports, a kind of phase shifter using air holes array in HMSIW is embodied in the power combiner. A K band 4-way in-phase power combiner is designed and fabricated to validate this design method. The simulated and measurement results show that the power combiner is well satisfied for K band high efficiency power combining.

articleTitle: Research of effective scheduling strategy on implementing high speed serial transmission switch module
abstract: This paper advance a system construct method about high speed serial transmission switch module. This module can exchange data between PCI-E and RapidIO, PCI-E and Fibre, RapidIO and Fibre. Aiming at high effective transmission. This paper advance a task scheduling optimization strategy and describe the principle in detail. This paper implement prototype, which can exchange data effectively in different protocol. In the end this paper finish the test about the prototype and the result of the test shows that the system construct method and the task scheduling optimization strategy are reasonable and feasible.

articleTitle: RCS computation of engine by parallel higher-order MoM with out-of- core technique
abstract: In this paper, a Method of Moments with Higher-Order basis functions (HOBMoM), parallel implementation based on Message Passing Interface (MPI) and Out-of-Core technology (OOC) has been proposed to compute the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of an aircraft's engine. The block-partitioned parallel scheme for the large dense MoM matrix is designed to achieve excellent load balancing and high parallel efficiency. Because of the bottleneck of the RAM limitation, the out-of-core technology is employed. Some numerical results demonstrate that the Higher-Order basis used in this paper is superior to the conventional RWG basis and is capable of solving various electrically large problems such as the computation of RCS.

Author Keywords: Method of Moments (MoM) with higher order basis functions

articleTitle: Doppler ambiguity resolution based on random sparse probing pulses
abstract: A novel method for solving Doppler ambiguous problem based on compressed sensing (CS) theory is proposed in this paper. According to the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP) of the CS sensing matrix, a sparse pulse train are randomly extracted from traditional fixed repetition frequency pulses, and then a random perturbation item is added to the transmitting time of each selected pulse. The received signals after matched filtering can be viewed as randomly sparse sampling from the traditional fixed-PRF (pulse repetition frequency) echo signals. With the transmitting time sequence, a sensing matrix can be built and the whole target echo could be recovered via CS recovery algorithms. Through refining the sensing matrix, which is equivalent to increase the sampling frequency of target characteristic, the Doppler unambiguous range is enlarged. Compared with traditional methods, the proposed method only requires transmitting a few sparse probing pulses to achieve a larger Doppler frequency unambiguous range and can reduce the consumption of the radar time resources. The radar dwell scheduling only needs slight adjustment, thus our proposed method has great value of practical application.

articleTitle: Robust blind beamforming with arbitrary sidelobe shape for MIMO radar based on second order cone program
abstract: A new robust algorithm based on second order cone program, which can get arbitrary sidelobe shape, is proposed for the problem of high sidelobe caused by nonuniform array configuration for MIMO radar. The new method firstly estimate the signal steering vector blindly by the numeration of fourth order Cumulants. By imposing a bound on the error between the estimated signal steering vector and actual signal steering vector and adding multiple quadratic inequality constrains to sidelobe regions, the method, suppressing interference efficiently and retaining antenna gain of expectant aspect, achieves desired and controllable arbitrary sidelobe shape in the presence of vector mismatches. The optimization model can be converted into convex second order cone programming issue, which can be solved using the existing interior method. Computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed method can overcome vector mismatches caused by blind estimation of the signal steering vector and array position, which achieves the lower arbitrary sidelobe shape and gets better robustness and higher SINR. Simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: Considerations of spaceborne SAR system design
abstract: This paper analyses the application requirements of spaceborne SAR system, and provides the general design flow of spaceborne SAR system design. Some spaceborne SAR systems are researched, which either have been launched successfully in recent years or being manufactured. The concerned technical factors of system design are contrasted and analysed, such as orbit design, configuration design, power system design, attitude and orbital control, SAR payload specifications and data transmission. Some unique technical problems of spaceborne SAR system design are summarized, and solutions and advises are put forward based on technology actuality.

articleTitle: Azimuth resolution improvement of spaceborne SAR images with nearly non-overlapped Doppler bandwidth
abstract: This paper deals with the azimuth resolution improvement problems via the coherent combination of the SAR images with nearly zero-overlapped Doppler bandwidth, which corresponding to large along-track baseline. Prior to the combination of the images, the phase bias contributions from the atmospheric propagation delays and baseline measurement errors should be calibrated. The interferogram of the azimuth pre-filtered SAR images are adopted in the classical method, whose performance falls down when the overlapped spectra comes to zero. In this paper, the maximum sharpness optimization is adopted to deal this situation. The proposed method has been tested by processing the real data.

articleTitle: Resolving targets using space-time snapshot based on GLRT algorithm
abstract: Around the space-time snapshot signal model of the array antenna radar receiver, this paper presents a small interval (less than the limit of Rayleigh resolution) target resolution algorithm, and the limit of space-time two-dimensional (2D) resolution. According to statistical detection theories, it presents a local optimum detection strategy based on generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) to detect the existence of one single target or two close to each ( whether there is one single target of two contained in echoes). Meanwhile, through the performance analysis of the proposed detector, we deduce the explicit relationship between the space-time 2D parameter difference of the minimum resolution and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The forecast and real performance of the presented detector is verified by Monte-Carlo simulation and the performance of resolving ability is compared with 2D MUSIC approach.

articleTitle: Image registration of SAR and optical image based on feature points
abstract: Image registration is one of the basic image processing operations in image understanding. Optical camera and SAR are widely used in mapping and remote sensing. By registering two images, the fusion of multimodality information becomes possible. Transformation model is the most important factor in image registration based on feature points. The authors systematically introduce the principle of optical imagery and propose the geometric model of SAR imaging. Prove that projective transformation is the best model for SAR and optical image registration both in theory and practice.

articleTitle: Statistical resolution limit based on Cramer-Rao bound
abstract: An extension study of Smith's result is proposed. An exact Cramer-Rao bound expression of frequency difference is deduced. The Cramer-Rao bound expression is analyzed asymptotically for the closely spaced targets case. A general close form of statistical resolution limit (SRL) is provided based on the asymptotic results. The SRL proposed is a function of power ratio, phase difference, and SNR. It is found that the power ratio and phase difference affect the relationship between SRL and SNR severely in further examination of the effect of the power ratio and phase difference. Maximum likelihood Estimation (MLE) simulation results shows that the variance of the MLE is close to the CRB in the resolvable area, but departs the CRB at the predicted resolution limit point. Simulation results proved that the statistical resolution limit proposed is correct and accurate.

articleTitle: Modified hybrid digital correlation algorithm for highly squint SAR image formation
abstract: This paper proposed a modified hybrid digital correlation algorithm for the highly squint SAR signal processing. Based on the two-step range migration correction, the modified hybrid digital correlation algorithm was efficient. Thus, it was a good choice of focusing processing in highly squint SAR. Simulation results validated the algorithm proposed in the paper.

articleTitle: High resolution range profile with promoted sparsity and refined grid
abstract: A high resolution range profile (HRRP) method via compressed sensing (CS) with re-weighted 11 minimization is proposed. Since the weighted CS model has a better representation of the true sparse description than that of the general 11 norm based CS model, the proposed compressive HRRP exhibits a remarkable suppression of the noise influence when dealing with a high background noise circumstance. To reduce the computational complexity, a refinement method is drawn. The experiment results demonstrate that, compared with classical CS, our improved CS model can achieve a higher resolution range profile while its computation time is relatively small.

articleTitle: Robust High-Resolution and Wide-Swath SAR imaging based on topelitz preprocessing
abstract: Along-track multi-channel spaceborne SAR system, capable of overcoming the minimum antenna area constraint, is promising in High-Resolution and Wide-Swath imaging by suppressing Doppler ambiguity. The space-time adaptive processing (STAP) is one of the effective methods to suppress the Doppler ambiguity. However, the lack of snapshots and channel errors will degrade its performance greatly. In this paper, a new channel calibration method based on topelitz preprocessing is proposed, which is capable of overcoming these non-ideal factors. Finally, the simulations confirm the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Improved Capon Beamforming Algorithm by using inverse covariance matrix calculation
abstract: Capon Beamforming Algorithm involves calculating inverse covariance matrix. It's complex to calculate inverse matrix in engineering applications. On the basis of summary of distribution of covariance matrix elements, an improved inverse covariance matrix calculating method is proposed. Simulation shows that the improved algorithm achieves the same accuracy with original algorithm as reducing the computational complexity.

articleTitle: Waveform design for MIMO over-the-horizon radar detection in signal dependent clutter and colored noise
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of waveform design for a multiple-input multiple-output over-the-horizon (MIMO-OTH) radar system corrupted by colored Gaussian noise and signal dependent clutter. The discrete prolate spheroidal (DPS) sequences are applied to construct the waveforms as their band-limited property is suitable for addressing the operational frequency limitations of the MIMO-OTH radar. Optimum waveforms (possibly nonorthogonal) are designed to maximize the target detection performance of the MIMO-OTH radar system under the constraint of fixed total transmitted energy. The effects of the spatial and temporal correlation of the noise are analyzed.

articleTitle: Azimuth spectrum reconstruction using FrFT for formation-flying satellites SAR
abstract: Spatial azimuth samples provided by formation-flying satellites are almost irregularly spaced and can be represented as a periodic non-uniformly sampling because of the influence of various factors; consequently, traditional imaging algorithm produces unsatisfactory results. In order to solve this problem, the theory of Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) is introduced and azimuth spectrum reconstruction algorithm based on FrFT for formation-flying satellites SAR is proposed. Not only the proposed reconstruction algorithm can reconstruct uniform signal spectrum along the track from periodic non-uniformly sampled signal, it can also be utilized to carry out high-resolution and wide-swath simultaneously for formation-flying satellites SAR system. Finally, simulations are presented to verify the theory.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of LFM signal via compressive sensing
abstract: A novel approach for parameter estimation of LFM signal via compressive sensing is proposed. Considering that LFM signal is sparse in time-frequency domain, compressive sensing technique is used to reconstruct short time Fourier transform of LFM signal. In the reconstruction process, practical sampling rate is considerably lower than Nyquist rate and hence the implementation complexity can be reduced significantly. The Radon transform is then used to search for line in time-frequency plane and estimate parameters. Simulation results show that this approach is capable of estimating parameters of LFM signal using limited numbers of measurements acquiring at sub-Nyquist rate and such a sampling saving at high Nyquist rates (several GHz) would be immense.

articleTitle: Adaptive waveform design in random stepped frequency radar
abstract: Random stepped frequency (RSF) radar, whose carrier frequencies randomly hop pulse by pulse, improves the range-Doppler ambiguity and produces excellent electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) ability. Sparse Recovery technique improves the sensing performance of RSF radar by exploiting the sparsity of the observed targets. In this paper, a cognitive mechanism is implemented to further enhance the RSF radar. The transmitted waveforms, i.e. frequency-hopping codes, are adaptively designed to coordinate with the targets. We choose to minimize the Cramer-Rao bound on sparse recovery errors as the waveform-design criterion, and devise two corresponding algorithms. Simulations are performed, whose results demonstrate that the proposed cognitive mechanism introduces significant improvements on the performance of targets recovery.

articleTitle: A channel equalization approach using the spatial correlation property of clutters
abstract: For the multi-channel ground moving target indication (GMTI) system in the aircraft platform, the channel mismatch will degrade the detection probability for moving targets, since the correlation property of the clutter between channels is decreased. In this paper, a novel channel equalization approach is presented, which uses the spatial correlation property of ground clutters from multi-channels to evaluate the mismatch errors without the signal calibration component, reducing the complexity of the multi-channel airborne SARGMTI system. Theoretical analysis shows that the response of the estimated equalizer is close to the practical mismatch errors when the clutter-to-noise ratio (CNR) of the data is high enough. Furthermore, experimental results using measured data are given to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Scale characteristic of sea surface backscattering echo
abstract: This paper deals with the azimuthal sea clutter, namely sea clutter from a series of different radar azimuths. The purpose is to demonstrate the fractal property of the azimuthal sea clutter. In detail, the random walk model of sea clutter is introduced, and then the criterion of judging the fractal property of sea clutter is presented. By analyzing the real azimuthal sea clutter data from X-band navigation radar, it is found that the fractal property of the azimuthal sea clutter is closely related to the grazing angle and the sea state. Low sea state (calm sea surface) and very low grazing angle will result in the non-fractal performance of the azimuthal sea clutter.

articleTitle: Analysis of Clutter characteristics of Integrated Sensor Is Structure
abstract: Clutter characteristics of Integrated Sensor Is Structure (ISIS) are researched in this paper. Conclusions are deduced from numerical simulation of the radiation pattern and clutter distribution. Taylor weighting depresses the amplitude of clutter from side-lobe, and also depresses the amplitude of the target echo from main-lobe. Large aperture provides high antenna gain, but results in very narrow radar beam which is adverse to large-scale scan. Clutter distribution is related to locomotion character of platform and operational parameters of radar. It is necessary to choose appropriate operational parameters to detect target in clutter.

articleTitle: Signal characteristics analysis of GEO SAR
abstract: Due to the advantage of one day repeating-cycle period, Geosynchronous SAR (GEO SAR) has caused much more increasing attention in the academia and industry. In order to describe GEO SAR accurately, the signal characteristics including synthetic aperture, temporal resolution, imaging swath, satellite velocity and resolution improvement factor in GEO SAR are analysed in this paper. Based on the signal characteristics, the signal processing methods of chirp scaling algorithm, range Doppler algorithm and Back Projection algorithm are applied for GEO SAR imaging. By analysis of simulation results of point target imaging, it is found that Back Projection algorithm can produce the best point target imaging. At last, some typical applications of GEO SAR are also introduced. The study on GEO SAR has remarkable economic benefits and social effects.

articleTitle: High resolution LASAR 3-D imaging based on IAA algorithm
abstract: This paper concerns the super-resolution method for linear array synthetic aperture radar (LASAR). Limited by the length of the linear array, the cross-track resolution is always low. Furthermore, with the large number of along-track (AT) samples, the computational complexity is always very large. To overcome the former disadvantage, this paper employs an iterative adaptive approach (IAA) algorithm to reconstruct the scatterer's reflectivity in the AT and cross-track (CT) direction. To overcome the last disadvantage, by exploiting the sparse characteristics of the 3D scene, this paper applies a sparse array antenna in LASAR system to reduce the samples. Compared with the traditional method, the presented IAA methods can obtain a better resolution. The simulation and experimental results validate the effective of performance of the presented method.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler analysis of nutation target in ballistic midcourse
abstract: Micro-Doppler signatures of ballistic targets are of great potential for discriminating the missile warheads and decoys in ballistic midcourse. Considering the rotary symmetrical coning target, the model of nutation is built and the mathematics of micro-Doppler signatures for different scattering centers are developed. Based on the electromagnetic scattering model, computer simulations are conducted by using the time-frequency analysis technique SPWVD to verify theoretic formulas, and the results show that simulated micro-Doppler signatures are coincident with theoretic formulas.

articleTitle: High-resolution FM stepped-frequency miniSAR system
abstract: System design technique of high-resolution FM stepped-frequency (FM-SF) SAR system is investigated in this paper. High-resolution SAR system is implemented through narrow sub-band, multi stepped-frequency and high pulse repetition frequency technique. Double phased lock loops operate alternatively and generate stepped local oscillator. Non-linear phase error and starting sampling range error are estimated and compensated to improve the performance of pulse compression result. System performance is verified through airborne experiment and can satisfy high resolution imaging requirement.

articleTitle: New method for passive radar seeker to antagonize non-coherent radar decoy
abstract: Using super resolution direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm is an effective method for passive radar seeker (PRS) to antagonize non-coherent radar decoy. A novel DOA estimation algorithm is proposed to estimate the two-dimensional (2-D) arrival angles of multisource by using a uniformly circular array (UCA) of crossed dipoles. By exploiting the polarization diversity of the signals, PRS improves the resolution in condition of closely spaced noncoherent sources for both chirp signals and phase modulated (PM) signals, and offers superior performance as the polarization changes. Simulation results verify the capability and correctness of the new method.

articleTitle: Doppler ambiguity correction using energy accumulation
abstract: The coherent integration of multiple pulses can improve the detection performance of weak targets. However, in the process of coherent integration, serious echo envelope migration exists when the target moves fast. A method named keystone transform has been proposed to solve this problem. Nevertheless, for wideband radars, the problem of energy dispersal increases the difficulties of Doppler ambiguity searching. Thus, in this paper, a Doppler ambiguity searching method based on energy accumulation is proposed. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by the simulations.

articleTitle: Research on the method of radar-to-ESM track correlation
abstract: This paper proposes a new method to realize the track correlation of Radar and ESM. Firstly, the coarse correlation rule is set up via the first-order Taylor series expansion and a coarse association function based on the geometry of radar and ESM. Then, the fine correlation matrix is set up by accumulating the historical information of the coarse correlation matrix. It is found that the coarse correlation threshold is only related with ESM measurement error. Finally, the simulation results show that the new proposed algorithm can effectively improve the correlation performance.

articleTitle: Multiple manoeuvring targets tracking via GM-PHD and IMM-SB/MHT
abstract: Probability hypothesis density (PHD) filter, which propagates the PHD or the first order moment instead of the full multitarget posterior density, is a promising multi-target tracking algorithm under density clutter capable of tracking random spawn and birth targets based on random finite set (RFS) statistics. Gaussian Mixture probability hypothesis density (GM-PHD) filter derivated from PHD filter plays an important role for PHD to practical applications. The interacting multiple model (IMM) technique can not be used in PHD and its derivations because the densities in PHD are not necessarily Gaussian and might be multi-modal. This paper proposes a combining technique which integrates linear Gaussian jump Markov system GM-PHD (LGJMS-GMPHD), structured branching multiple hypothesis tracking (SB/MHT) and IMM approach for multiple maneuvering targets tracking. First, LGJMS-GM-PHD is acted as pre-filter which eliminates most of clutter in measurements. Then, a gating technique is used according to state output of the LGJMS-GM-PHD, measurement which locates in the gate is a candidate measurement for branch and update under the framework of SB/MHT. Last, IMM is used to estimate the state of the maneuvering target in the framework of SB/MHT. This combining approach takes use of the advantages of LGJMS-GM-PHD, SB/MHT and IMM which can perform multiple maneuvering targets tracking under density clutter effectively.

Author Keywords: Gaussian Mixture probability hypothesis density (GM-PHD) filter

articleTitle: ISAR imaging of space objects based on stepped frequency modulation
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging using stepped frequency modulation (SFM) signal is an important approach to achieve 2-dimensional high resolution. The range imaging method and the motion compensation method in ISAR imaging based on SFM signal are presented. The antidromic discarding method is adopted in range imaging to find a suitable starting point and to spell the range profiles. The least squares interpolation method based on prior information is used to estimate object's range and velocity. The processing flow of the ISAR imaging approach base on the Range-Doppler method is showed. The final simulation results demonstrate that this approach can obtain high quality and high resolution 2-dimensional images.

articleTitle: Radar capability incorporated into signal processor
abstract: Time and costs are of great concern for designing a simulator. It's not always wise to introduce an extra simulator to debug and test a signal processing system. In this paper, considering the characteristics of the signal processor, we propose a novel method of incorporating radar echo simulation capability into the signal processor with no extra hardware resource needed. Detailed mathematical modelling of the exact radar echo is first presented. Then the design of echo simulation function is elaborated. Taking into account the very short development time, the experimental results are very satisfying.

articleTitle: Polarimetric characteristics of step frequency echo in through-wall-imaging
abstract: This paper concerns the theoretical analyzing about the information capacity and characteristics of the echo's polarimetric components, in through-the-wall scene, resorting to the polarimetric scatter matrix. The expressions of the four polarimetric components are proposed. Based on the reasoning, we deeply analyze the characteristics of each component and its effect on the imaging, detection and further process. Then some suggestions about optimal application of the polarimetric components are given. Experiment results validate this paper. What's more, the reasoning, in this paper, also applies to other signal format after simple transformation.

articleTitle: Derivative constraint-based householder multistage wiener filter for adaptive beamforming
abstract: Adaptive beamforming technology could perform excellent performance under ideal conditions. However, the severe performance loss would be caused by steering vector mismatch in practical systems. In order to avoid the performance deterioration, a reduced-rank derivative constraint-based householder multistage wiener filter is proposed for adaptive beamforming in this paper. In the proposed method, the derivative constraints are applied to generate constraint condition on the direction of expectation at first, adaptive processing is carried out based on the householder multistage wiener filter. The proposed method not only has the robustness for the steering vector mismatch between the actual and the presumed steering vector, but also reduces the computational complexity significantly due to the multistage wiener filter adaptive beamforming technique. At last, corresponding simulations are carried out to verify the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: A method of determining the direction of velocity space-variance in GEO SAR
abstract: Geosynchronous Earth Orbit Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) has the advantages of short repeat time, large coverage area and so on. For the long aperture time and high orbit height, the effect of velocity space-variance on GEO SAR is more severe than on Low Earth Orbit SAR (LEO SAR). However, the spatial variation of velocity is different in different directions, which will bring new challenge to the imaging process. This paper analyses the effect of velocity space-variance on GEO SAR and LEO SAR respectively, proposes a method to find the direction of velocity spacevariance. Finally, the correctness of this method is proved through imaging simulation.

articleTitle: The impact of step selection in NLMS algorithm on low velocity target detecting for passive radar
abstract: Normalized Least-Mean Squares (NLMS) algorithm is widely used in cancelling the direct path and multi-path interferences in the passive coherent location (PCL) radar systems. The value of the step size in the NLMS algorithm impacts on the output of the canceller, which leads to different performance of the target detection. This paper analyses the impacts of different step size on low velocity target detecting and proposes that the larger step size results in the gain loss of the low velocity target in the cross ambiguity function (CAP) of passive radar. And a novel target detection algorithm with variable threshold in the CAP is proposed, which can be used to detect the low velocity targets and high velocity targets at the same time even if the CAP surface has a big notch. The validity of the algorithm is verified by both the simulative and experimental results.

articleTitle: Estimation of number of signal sources in far separated sub-arrays
abstract: In this paper we study the estimation of the number of signal sources in a particular class of sparse linear array, characterized by several far separated sub-arrays. Since a large array aperture which is obtained with the sparse linear array can produces more robust reservation and very accurate angle estimates at a reasonable cost, but a key issue in these problems is the detection of the number of signals. We evaluate the performances of estimation and compare with the performances in a uniform linear array.

Author Keywords: Estimation of the number of signal sources

articleTitle: Task scheduling in the non-ideal topology
abstract: In the non-ideal topology, processors are not fully-connected and the data transmission cannot achieve fully-concurrency, so the schedule of IPCs (Inter Processor Communication) will affect the performance of parallel processing directly. However, traditional scheduling method usually ignored the scheduling of IPCs, or only schedule IPCs under the simple topologies. To solve this problem, the disadvantages of traditional task scheduling methods are analyzed, and a more practical method is put forward, which consists of three steps: first, build the topology model to describe the hardware system; second, define different IPC scheduling principles and for different interconnections between processors under the topology model; third, schedule tasks in the non-ideal topology by applying the IPC scheduling method into the DLS (Dynamic Level Scheduling) method. The test of three groups of random tasks with different CCR (Communication to Computation Radio) and the test of an actual signal processing algorithm, show that the method proposed in this paper achieves a better accuracy, and more suitable for the embedded parallel systems.

articleTitle: GPU-accelerated 3D compressive sensing CSAR imaging
abstract: In circular synthetic aperture radar (CSAR), radar collects data over a circular trajectory. This wide-angle non-linear collection geometry makes CSAR capable of obtaining both two-dimensional (2D) high resolution image and three-dimensional (3D) image. In this paper, compressive sensing technique is used in 3D CSAR imaging. Not only echo samples used in imaging are greatly reduced, but also the imaging results are with good performance. However, the consumed time of reconstruction is very long. In order to overcome this problem, graphic process unit (GPU) is furtherly used in 3D compressive sensing CSAR imaging in this paper. Simulation results show that GPU can improve the efficiency of the 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: An innovative subarray partition method based on genetic algorithm for linear arrays
abstract: Subarray technology is an effective solution to the “conflict of sum and difference” in a large array radar. However, the optimal subarray partition method is a difficult problem both in the theoretic and practices. By exploring the advantage of genetic algorithm, a method, to optimize the subarray configuration in monopulse application, is proposed in this paper. The innovative method is subtly designed and discussed in-depth. Numerical results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the innovative method.

articleTitle: A study of MMW collision avoidance radar system for trains
abstract: Collision avoidance radar for trains is significant for safe transportation. In order to realize a low cost collision avoidance radar and high performance of azimuth accuracy, we have developed MMW (millimetre wave) radar, which employs switched phased array and frequency stepped technology. This paper analyses the radiation patterns of transmitting/receiving antennas and compensation method for amplitude/phase errors of synthetic wideband frequency stepped radar. To confirm the operation of the radar, low cost millimetre-wave collision avoidance radar was fabricated. Lots of experiments confirmed a high azimuth and range resolution.

articleTitle: RCS calculation using parallel PO on supercomputer
abstract: Physical optics (PO) method can deal with the problem of RCS calculation, while the calculation time of this method will still be very long for targets of huge electrical size. Utilizing the platform of the National Supercomputing Center in Tianjin (rank first on Top 500 in November 2010), the parallel PO method is used to calculate the RCS of electrically large targets. Furthermore, some benchmarks about parallel efficiency of the code are tested on the supercomputer platform. The results indicate that a linear speedup can be achieved.

articleTitle: Sparse passive radar imaging based on FM stations using the U-ESPRIT for moving target
abstract: This paper studies the passive radar imaging system based on Frequency Modulated (FM) stations. Firstly, we establish the imaging model for moving target which consists of multiple FM stations and one receiver. Although movement information brings improvement of resolution, similarly to ISAR, but the shortage of wavenumber domain filling also causes the failure in imaging under little stations condition, so we consider using the sparse recovery techniques to realize imaging. However, in actual radar system, some previous CS methods probably suffer from off-grid point effect, which causes performance degradation of the methods. Therefore, based on the theories of Xampling and the finite rate of innovation (FRI), we propose a high-resolution sparse imaging method to overcome the problems stated above, which utilizes the unitary estimating signal parameters through rotational invariance techniques (U-ESPRIT) and the cross point searching technique (CPST). Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method and the related analysis.

articleTitle: Micro-motion analysis based on HRRP sequence
abstract: Since micro-motion of a target will affect the positions and phases of scatters in high resolution range profiler (HRRP), the methods of micro-motion extraction from the signals of range gates cannot be used. According to the variation features of scatter position, we treat the HRRPs as image sequence and an improved Viterbi algorithm is used to track and isolate the range-gate histories of scatters. Then the time-frequency transform and spectral analysis methods are performed to analyze the micro-motion characteristics of each scatter. The proposed algorithm is verified via simulation data and its performance under noisy environment is analyzed.

articleTitle: Three dimensional ISAR imaging for human being
abstract: Millimeter wave imaging techniques for full body scanner is becoming increasingly important to detect concealed body-worn threats. A new configuration of full body scanner is designed in this paper. It utilizes human movement and standing linear array to form a planar synthetic aperture, which basically pertains to inverse synthetic aperture radar. Human movement is controlled by powerwalk, so the velocity of human is known. A three dimensional ISAR imaging algorithm is proposed and system parameters design is also discussed. Imaging result of human point model is given to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of 60GHZ MMIC LNA in mHEMT technology
abstract: A 60GHz MMIC Low-noise Amplifier (LNA) was designed and simulated using OMMIC's 130nm GaAs mHEMT process. Based on the simulating results of Momentum, the main features of the LNA designed can be summarized as following: the three-stage LNA can reach 17dB average gain with less than ±0.5dB ripple in the operating frequency range (from 56GHz to 63GHz) and the noise figure is less than 3.15dB. Total chip size is 3000um×2000um.

articleTitle: Simple systematic frequency reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna
abstract: A simple, efficient, reconfigurable sweeping frequency, single feed, fork shaped microstrip antenna is presented in this paper. The reconfigurability of frequency is presented by incorporating pin diode, in series, to switch the successive operating frequencies considerably by changing the antenna effective length. The proposed antenna sweeps frequency along Ku band; provided in this work six resonant frequencies, namely (13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17 & 18 GHz), with nearly fixed radiation pattern, constant gain more than (7dB) and return loss less than (-10 dB) over the entire band. The proposed antenna shape presented can be used over any frequency band and can be applied to various applications. The proposed antenna is explained and simulation results are presented. The antenna is simulated by using both Zeland's MoM based IE3D tool and HFSS, the simulation results are identical hence validate the design.

articleTitle: Improved two-step algorithm in geosynchronous SAR
abstract: In Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR), the very large swath width makes the classical line trajectory model invalid and the imaging parameters space-variant. In this paper, an accurate slant range model is firstly given for GEO SAR. Next, an improved two-step algorithm which can overcome the difficulties introduced by space-variance of imaging parameters is proposed. Furthermore, simulation results fully verify the correctness and effectiveness of the derived algorithm.

articleTitle: Antenna area constraint in GEO SAR
abstract: Inclined geosynchronous Earth orbit synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) is seriously affected by Earth rotation because of its identical angular velocity with the Earth rotation. Therefore, the composition motion of GEO SAR and the illuminated target is extremely complicated because of the inclined orbit geometry. Hence the analysis methods of stripmap mode are no longer suitable for GEO SAR. The classical SAR minimum antenna area criterion fails either. This paper analyses the calculation of the antenna area constraint in GEO SAR based on all the possible existing cases in one running orbit. Finally, a simulation is given out based on a set of typical GEO SAR parameters.

articleTitle: Study on along-track motion compensation for FMCW SAR
abstract: Since the duty cycle is one for frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and the approach of pulse repeat frequency (PRF) online adjustment could not be adopted any more, a new approach of compensating the along track motion error is proposed without computational taxing interpolation. The distortion of SAR image derived from motion error is analyzed and the motion error is separated into inter-pulse and intra pulse error. The flow chart of compensation along track is eventually presented in this paper. Simulation result shows the method proposed is effective and practical.

articleTitle: Enhancements of the satellite selection method for multi-constellation GNSS using convex geometry
abstract: With the gradual establishment of the multi-constellation navigation system, the receiver's information processing is faced with challenges. Then the idea of packet processing has been widely used for the satellite selection and integrity monitoring of multiple systems, which many papers have put forward. Packet processing for multi-system can not only accelerate the speed of the satellite selection, but also improve the probability and the number of fault detection. The convex hull algorithm is selected for low calculation. when the satellites were grouped in the processing, the improved algorithm introduces the classic parity vector method to detect and exclude fault satellites. After the packet processing and the final integration,the convex hull algorithm will give the optimal and healthy satellite constellation. Finally, the algorithm not only integrates satellite selected algorithm and RAIM for the multi-constellation,but also solves the shortcomings that the fault of selected satellites will seriously influence the positioning after the satellites were selected. A significant reference value is provided for consumer electronics applications of navigation, and the compatibility of less channel's receiver under multi-constellation.

articleTitle: An ambiguity-resovled correction algorithm of phase interferometer based on Kalman prediction
abstract: An ambiguity-resolved correction algorithm based on Kalman prediction (ARCKP) aims to correct errors in resolving phase ambiguity of multi-baseline phase interferometer. The algorithm takes Kalman predictive values as criteria that ambiguity resolved are right or not and uses the predictive values to correct error positions. Analysing judgment threshold of outlier and comparing with exiting algorithms. Simulation results indicate that the new algorithm can better identify outliers and correct data when longer processing interval and higher dynamic exists.

articleTitle: A realization of convenient structure with electrical coupling in coaxial cavity
abstract: Electrical coupling is essential in some RF circuits. In this paper, we present a convenient mixed-coupling structure between coaxial cavities, and the ratio of electric coupling coefficient to magnetic coupling coefficient could be tuned easily. As a result, an electric coupling effect without the probe can be achieved in coupling coaxial resonators. For validating the theory, the electric coupling structure is used to realize a four-order cross-coupled filter, and the measured results match well with the theoretical prediction. Especially, there are three transmission zeros near the pass band.

articleTitle: Phase error analysis in GEO SAR imaging based on MSR
abstract: Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) is a kind of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) running on the geosynchronous orbit with a certain inclination. Because of the high orbit, it has different characters compared with the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) SAR. This paper consists of four folders: firstly, the unsuitableness of linear trajectory model in GEO SAR imaging is proved; secondly, the slant range model based on elliptic orbit is given, and the phase errors of cubic and quartic polynomial models are calculated, respectively; thirdly, the relationships of the phase error and inclination, the phase error and eccentricity in special areas are analysed; finally, the method of series reversion (MSR) is introduced in GEO SAR imaging to validate the conclusions.

articleTitle: New method for detection and parameter estimation of Stlfm signal
abstract: In order to reduce the computation complexity of parameter estimation for STLFM signals, a new algorithm based on Ambiguity Function slice and Fractional Fourier Transform is presented. Firstly, the frequency rate is estimated through one AF slice at fixed time-delay of observation signals, and then getting the best order of FrFT. Finally, the other parameters, including frequency modulation bandwidth, frequency modulation cycle and center frequency, is estimated by twice FrFT. The whole processing just need three times FFT computation complexity and can estimate all the STLFM signal parameters. Simulation results show that the algorithm can estimate the parameters of chirp signal quickly and effectively.

articleTitle: Super-resolution image reconstruction algorithm based on double sparse representation
abstract: Aiming at the current requirements of image reconstruction in the actual applications, by studying the super-resolution image reconstruction and the theory of sparse representation, this paper proposes a super-resolution image reconstruction algorithm based on double sparse representation. This paper also makes some comparative experiments with the algorithm based on single sparse representation. The experiment results show that the reconstruction results of our algorithm are better than the results of super-resolution image reconstruction algorithm based on single sparse presentation.

articleTitle: CRB of target location and velocity estimation in MIMO radar
abstract: A model of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar combining widely separated and colocated antennas is developed and the joint Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) for estimating the target location and the target velocity are derived for this type of MIMO radar system in order to analyze its estimation performance and the factors affecting on the performance. Simulation results are presented and illustrate that MIMO radar with more separated subarrys consisting of colocated antenna elements has better and more stable performance on the location and velocity estimation for a moving target.

articleTitle: Resonance-region target detection with wideband VHF radar
abstract: VHF radar shows great promise in detecting stealth targets, since it works in resonance regions. Wideband VHF radar, as a new radar system, has an enormous potential. In this paper, target detection with wideband VHF radar that compensates for the fluctuation of targets' RCS between different frequencies in the resonance region is introduced. The Boeing 747-200 model and the Predator model were designed for the study, and the aircrafts were studied in the 40~80MHz frequency band. Results show that: (1) the wideband detection is better than the narrowband single frequency detection; and (2) for greatly fluctuating targets, the wideband detection is better than the multi-frequency detection.

articleTitle: The study of mono-pulse angle measurement based on digital array radar
abstract: In digital array radar (DAR) system, digital mono-pulse techniques with digital beam forming method are widely used recently. Firstly, this paper introduces the theory of amplitude-comparison of sum and difference lobes and phase and sum-difference digital mono-pulse. Secondly, noise and element amplitude and phase errors which affect the accuracy of angle measurement are analysed and simulated. Lastly, the simulation results and measurements are compared and some proposals for engineering are given.

articleTitle: Ground-based SAR imaging based on improved Range-Doppler algorithm
abstract: Ground-based SAR, which uses a rotated antenna to form the synthesize aperture, is used to detect the small static objects on the ground. The high resolution image algorithm is proposed based on Range Doppler imaging method, and the range cell migration is analyzed. A range migration correction kernel function in azimuth frequency domain is formed based on the analysis of the formation of range migration; the simulation results show that the algorithm is efficiency.

articleTitle: A novel CAEMD filtering algorithm for SAR image speckle noise
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a very important remote sensing technology instrument, as it has the notable characteristic of obtaining data under all-time and all-weather, but the coherent imaging theory leads to speckle noise which brings a lot of difficulty for its applications and interpretation. From the brought mechanism of speckle noise and the characteristic of experience mode decomposition (EMD), a new smoothing speckle noise method is proposed based on coherence and experience mode decomposition (CAEMD) for SAR images. The new method not only can hold the detailed information, but also can reduce speckle noise. Because the coherent operation can enhance target information and the EMD operation can keep down the background information. Some different SAR images and different reduce noise methods are used to perform comparative experiments, and results show that the CAEMD filtering method is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Data association method comparison with amplitude information
abstract: In addition to the spatial location information of the target obtained by the sensors for data association, other information about the target features is also included. Two already known methods which applied amplitude information to data association, amplitude likelihood function method and amplitude state vector method, and their performance are analyzed in this paper. Then we propose a new method named relative amplitude function based data association approach, which chooses the measurement whose amplitude value is nearest to the predicted one. Finally, the simulation of MHT with amplitude information illustrates the effectiveness of proposed method, which can effectively improve the performance for data association under dense clutter.

articleTitle: Imaging of space targets in FMCW-ISAR
abstract: Combining Frequency Modulation Continuous Wave (FMCW) and Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR), FMCW-ISAR is more practical with low cost, low power, small volume for short distance targets. However, the continuous echo signals in FMCW-ISAR system lead to dechirp distortion phenomenon during the process of dechirp for far-distance targets, especially for the space targets. In this paper, a signal model is proposed to study the image processing of space targets in FMCW-ISAR system. The effects of dechirp distortion which can be ignored for short-distance targets are analyzing for the first time. Double images of a target appear after imaging because of the distortion which decreases the resolution. A method is proposed to correct the distortion by translating the current received signal according to the acquired reference distance. The simulation results validate the theoretical analysis conclusions and the effectiveness of the proposed method for the distortion correction.

articleTitle: A new maneuvering target tracking method for HPRF radars
abstract: A maneuvering target tracking method for the high pulse-repetition frequency (HPRF) radars has to deal with two problems range ambiguity and maneuvering uncertainty. Therefore, it can not be achieved by the traditional maneuvering target tracking methods directly. A new maneuvering target tracking method for HPRF radars is proposed to realize range ambiguity resolving and maneuvering target tracking simultaneously. The maneuvering target tracking on the condition of range ambiguity is converted to a hybrid filtering problem by considering PIN and its incremental variable as target states. Then, interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with current statistical model (CSM) is given to realize the hybrid state estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to the existing multiple hypothesis method in terms of tracking accuracy and computation time.

articleTitle: A Bayesian method for weak target tracking aided by strong target
abstract: Weak target tracking in multiple target tracking (MTT) scenario is a challenging problem for its poor observation. In the paper, the method for weak target tracking aided by the information of strong target is proposed. The new method is derived with Bayesian framework. Compared with traditional MTT method, it is proved that the proposed tracking method for the weak target owns three aspects benefits, which are the estimate accuracy, convergence velocity and steady tracking time.

articleTitle: Target tracking with infrared imaging and millimetre-wave radar sensor
abstract: Two commonly used tracking fusion methods for Kalman filter-based multi-sensor data fusion which are weighed cross-covariance fusion and augmented measurement fusion are analysed in this paper. Based on tracking fusion of infrared sensor and millimetre wave Radar ,the fused states and measurements are compared with individual estimates. Results are presented using Monte Carlo simulation by two given virtual trajectories which show that: (1)the two fusion methods are functionally equivalent if the sensors used for data fusion have identical measurement matrix;(2)the obtained joint state-vector estimate is better than the individual sensor-based estimate. Also presented are the possible reason caused the bias between individual position estimate and true followed by the analysis of the computational advantages of each method.

articleTitle: A novel method for occlusion modeling and micro-doppler analysis of truck target
abstract: Trucks are widely used in transportation or on battlefield. Hence, the research on recognition of truck targets has great military and economic value. Micro-Doppler of running wheels is an important signature of trucks. In the paper, based on scatterer model, under high frequency radar system, taking the relative position of radar and truck into consideration, the occlusion model of truck is established by applying the Painter's algorithm, then the variation of the micro-Doppler with respect to azimuth, depression angle, velocity and acceleration is analyzed, which is the fundament of signature extraction and recognition for truck targets. The effectiveness of the method is proved by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Detection of tree roots and root biomass estimation based on ground penetrating radar with high accuracy positioning system
abstract: A new procedure for detection of tree roots and root biomass estimation by using a promising Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) system with high accuracy positioning system was proposed. This system acquires the accurate antenna position and fuses it with the GPR data, and then a three dimensional (3D) data cube can be obtained. After analysing the acquired 3D cube in field measurement, some specific reflection characteristics of roots were summarized, and then a detection procedure was proposed to detect the root extension starting from the tree stump. This detection procedure could exclude the influence of the strong clutters and overcome the weak reflection from one part of the root which resulted from the error of antenna operation in the survey. In order to validate the performance of detection and estimation, one tree was excavated after the measurement. The detection result shows that the coarse roots whose diameters were more than 5cm could be detected correctly, and the extension of the detected roots was corresponding to the true scene. The diameter of roots was over estimated, and the detection procedure needs to be improved in order to reduce the biomass estimation error within 30 percent.

articleTitle: Constained adaptive monopulse algorithm based on sub-array
abstract: A constrained adaptive sum-difference monopulse algorithm based on sub-array is presented in this paper. Adaptive processing is first conducted for sum beam of each sub-array and then for difference beam of each sub-array by adding monopulse ratio constraint, which yields adaptive sum beam and constrained difference beam respectively. Since the monopulse ratio constraint is imposed on whole array during calculating adaptive weight of difference beam, the aperture loss due to sub-array is overcome. Moreover, the new algorithm can null the mainlobe jamming and sidelobe jamming effectively while keeping adaptive monopulse ratio undistorted, which improves the angle measurement accuracy. The simulation experiments demonstrated the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Time resource scheduling algorithm for multiple target tracking in jamming
abstract: An effective time resource scheduling is very important to improve resource utilization ratio and optimize performance in phased array radar. A mathematical model of time scheduling algorithm for multiple target tracking in jamming is proposed. The algorithm assigns sampling time associated to cost function, considering the desired accuracy, manoeuvring character, the threat of air attack target and electronic interfere. The optimal sampling time is calculated using Ant Colony Optimization method successfully. Combined with Interactive Multiple Models and Joint Probabilistic Data Association, the target's position is estimated for beam pointing. Simulation results show that the performance of multiple target tracking in jamming is improved.

articleTitle: Motion compensation for missile-borne frequency stepped chirp radar
abstract: Motion compensation is a key problem for frequency stepped chirp radar (FSCR) in realizing synthetic high range resolution. In this paper, a novel velocity estimation algorithm based on the waveform entropy (WE) of the Doppler amplitude spectrum is developed for missile-borne FSCR, in order to compensate the target echo's additional phase resulting from the motion between the radar and the target. Without altering the conventional radar waveform, the new method can accurately estimate the radial velocity between the radar and the target and can be implemented on the in-service radars. Moreover, the method can be used for the scenario of multi-target with different velocities. It will be shown that the algorithm can effectively estimate the radial velocity and reconstruct the distorted HRRP successfully. In addition, the anti-noise performance of the proposed algorithm is well and the computation burden is acceptable for real time signal processing.

articleTitle: Feature level fusion of SAR and optical image and MPSoC IMPLEMENTATION
abstract: SAR image and optical image are heterogeneous images, so the integration of these two types of images can take full advantage of their complementary characteristics to obtain more description of the information. For this application, this paper gives one SAR and optical image feature fusion algorithm and presents a multiprocessor SoC system based on this algorithm. The system uses a master-slave/pipeline structure to solve the problems of communication and synchronization among processors and implement the real time processing for the feature fusion system of SAR and optical image. Mentioned multiprocessor SoC is implemented on a single FPGA chip to achieve the miniaturized design of the feature fusion. This can be used in military and aerospace field.

articleTitle: A efficient design of a real-time FFT architecture based on FPGA
abstract: In this paper, for the need of FFT computation for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging algorithm, Radix-2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Singularities Delay Feedback (R2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>SDF) algorithm with good realtime performance and less resources occupation is adopted. And a fixed-point module and a floating-point module were verified respectively with the implementation of FPGA. Thus the paper discusses the structure of the FFT algorithm. Compare the resource occupation and the speed of the fixedpoint module and the floating-point module. Analyse the performance of the algorithm. At last complete the SAR imaging process with fixed-point FFT algorithm, therefore save resources and give full play to the advantages of the FPGA. R2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>SDF FFT need less resource, has high real-time performance, is suitable for VLSI implementation.

articleTitle: A novel range profiles splicing approach in stepped-frequency radars
abstract: The traditional stepped-frequency signal processing method, employing IFFT to obtain the synthetic high resolution range (HRR) profile, suffers from a limitation that the max unambiguous range extent is too short, which is determined by the frequency step size. Some range splicing algorithms have been developed to solve this problem. However, for moving targets, performances of these range splicing algorithms are degraded because of range-Doppler coupling. In this paper, a novel range splicing method is proposed specially for moving targets. It uses the maximum amplitude point to determine the location of splicing window, and uses the compare strategy to tolerate the bias of splicing window. Both theoretical analysis and simulation prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sea clutter simulation based on sea surface model and two-scale scattering model
abstract: The sea clutter simulation scheme is made based on the sea surface model and two-scale scattering model. the amplitude distribution of the sea clutter is analyzed,the result shows that the scheme used in the article could generate suitable sea clutter series,the simulated sea clutter is in accord with statistical properties of real one,the feasibility of the sea clutter simulation which uses the scheme and models in the article is also justified.

articleTitle: Hybrid orthogonal-phased array MIMO RADAR
abstract: Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) radar is a multiple aperture technology characterized by the ability to transmit diverse signals at each aperture. This is in contrast to traditional phased array radar whereby a single signals is transmitted with a phase shift applied at each element to enable steering of the transmit beampattern. The hybrid MIMO phased array radar (HMPAR) concept is an outgrowth of the monostatic MIMO construct, in which all sensors have the same view of the far field target which is known as colocated antenna. In the HMPAR, the full transmit array is partitioned into sub-arrays which can be electronically steered in different directions and driven by separate transmit waveforms, furthermore the configuration of the array into sub-arrays can be changed. In this paper it is supposed that antennas are colocated and it will be shown that how it is possible to build a desire beampattern by means of designing cross-correlation matrix of transmitted signals to sector the space with such a system.

articleTitle: Effects of ionospheric high-order dispersion and multiple scattering on space-based SAR imaging
abstract: The interest in the use of space-borne SAR at low-frequency for collecting earth biomass information such as forest structure, soil moisture and soil type has been increased. It is crucial to understand the potential effects of radio wave propagation due to the ionospheric perturbation. In this paper, we present some effects of ionosphere on space-borne SAR imaging, especially the higher-order dispersion of the background and random scattering of irregularities are considered. Both the analysis and numerical simulation have been investigated to get some useful conclusions.

articleTitle: Extended fractal analysis of sea clutter frequency spectrum
abstract: Extended self-similar (ESS) process, as a generalized fractional Brownian motion (fBm) process, characterizes rough surfaces by a series of extended Hurst exponents instead of one single Hurst parameter that is used in the fBm process. So the ESS process is able to provide more clues about the local roughness of the surface at different scales. In this paper, the ESS process is applied to modelling the sea clutter frequency spectrum, for the reason that (a) for coherent radar, the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) can be promoted effectively by Fourier transform (namely in frequency domain); (b) through Fourier transform, the self-similarity in time domain can be held in frequency domain in statistical sense. Then based on X-band real sea clutter data, the extended self-similarity and the local roughness of the sea clutter frequency spectrum at different scales are analyzed. The results show that at some specific scales the extended Hurst exponents are sensitive to the existence of a target. And this sensitivity is propitious to promoting the performance of detecting weak moving target within sea clutter.

articleTitle: A hybrid scheduling algorithm of high speed radar tracking system based on CAN bus
abstract: In order to meet the development of the information exchange on a high speed radar tracking system, a hybrid scheduling algorithm based on CAN bus is presented. It combines the static (DM, FPS) and dynamic (EDF, LLF) scheduling algorithm. Static scheduling algorithm has fixed priority and can simply be used. However, its priority cannot be changed, which means that deadline of critical messages cannot be guaranteed. Dynamic scheduling algorithm can efficiently improve bandwidth utilization and guarantee the transmission of real-time messages. A hybrid scheduling algorithm is introduced with CAN2.0B extended data frame protocol. Finally, the experiment is carried out on a real network environment. Experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the system transmission efficiency and reliability, and meet the requirement of real-time information exchange.

articleTitle: Modified range migration algorithm integrated with motion compensation for FMCW SAR
abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a new kind of imaging radar. Unlike traditional pulsed SAR, the FMCW signal is continuously transmitted at all times and, hence, the radar can no longer be considered as stationary during the signal transmission and reception, i.e. the “stop-and-go” approximation is not valid. This leads to the effect of Doppler frequency shift. This paper proposes a modified range migration algorithm (RMA) for FMCW SAR. The Doppler frequency shift is analyzed in detail and is corrected in the range time and azimuth Doppler domain. The algorithm maintains the high precision of RMA and motion compensation can be integrated in it conveniently. Simulation results are presented to show the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An algorithm for detection of hidden objects by passive/active radiometer
abstract: Detection of concealed weapons and explosives under people clothing is an actual task nowadays. Different active radar and passive radiometers systems that operate in mm and sub-mm (or THz) bands have been designed for screening passengers in airports. Their effectiveness is rather low at surveying people in outer clothing. The effectiveness could be improved by using dual passive-active radiometer. Such a system consists from the passive radiometer and active noise generator that emits in the same frequency band as the radiometer. The generator is working in stroboscopic mode of operation. This gives an opportunity to record two images (passive and active) simultaneously. An algorithm, that processes both images, has been proposed. It affords to reduce level of false alarms and to raise the contrast of detected objects.

articleTitle: Research on antenna stabilization technology of micro SAR system
abstract: Antenna stabilization technology of micro UAV-SAR system has been researched in this paper. An approach that using attitude information measured by INS-GPS strapped on the aircraft to aid gimbals to stabilize antenna pointing has been presented. Dynamical vibration of the vehicle is isolated through controlling two-axis stabilization loop(azimuth and elevation). A strategy that guarantees antenna pointing stable in geography coordinates has been presented. At last, the performance of the stabilization platform was proved by the airborne experiments.

articleTitle: New ground penetrating radar system for quantitative characterization of snow and sea ice
abstract: We examine the use of ground penetrating radar (GPR) to simultaneously estimate snow and ice thickness. Since velocity is essential for depth inversion, we developed an automatic common mid-point (CMP) measurement system, which can work in an ultra-wide band. Envelope velocity spectrum, robust in reflection identification, is used to estimate the dielectric permittivity and layer thickness from CMP datasets. We tested our system on a 50-m-long test line on a brackish lagoon, i.e. Lake Saroma, in Hokkaido, Japan, in February 2012. Compared with the ground truth, the snow and ice thickness estimations possess a good accuracy, with a respective mean absolute error of about 2 cm (12%) and less than 2 cm (4%), which verifies the accuracy of their dielectric permittivity estimation. Then the estimated two-layer velocity model obtained by interpolation was used to continuously estimate the snow and ice thickness from the common-offset (CO) GPR profile acquired by a commercial GPR system. The mean absolute errors of snow and ice thickness estimated from the CO profile are respectively, about 3 cm (18%) and less than 6 cm (14%). Our system and method appear capable of accurately measuring the dielectric permittivity and thickness of other layered media.

articleTitle: Range ambiguity suppression by azimuth phase coding in multichannel SAR systems
abstract: Among the techniques for range ambiguity suppression, the azimuth phase coding (APC) stands out for its effectiveness for point and distributed targets with low implementation complexity. After modulation to the transmitted signal and the corresponding demodulation to the received signal, the residual modulation phase of the ambiguity signal shifts its Doppler spectrum, so that the spectrum of the useful signal and that of the ambiguity are not exactly superimposed. This enables an azimuth filter to eliminate a part of the ambiguity power. If it is desired to get an ambiguity-free SAR image, the pulse reputation frequency (PRF) should be several times larger than the Doppler bandwidth of the desired Doppler spectrum, which is hard to be satisfied in high-resolution wide-swath spaceborne SAR systems. This paper introduces a method for range ambiguity suppression based on the APC technology in multichannel SAR systems when the PRF is only a bit larger than the Doppler bandwidth. After applying the APC technique, the space-time spectrum of the ambiguity swath is separated from that of the useful signal. In multichannel SAR systems, the desired 2-D spectrum and the spectrum of the ambiguity swath can be obtained simultaneously by using the position information of antenna phase centres. Conventional imaging algorithms can then be applied to both spectrums to obtain SAR images of the imaging area and the ambiguity swaths. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Dynamic polarimetric calibration using a single dual-polarized antenna polarimetric active radar calibrator
abstract: This paper designs a single rotatable dual-polarized antenna polarimetric active radar calibrator (PARC) and proposes a corresponding dynamic calibration polarimetric (DPC) method. The novel PARC simplifies the system equipment and optimises the antenna's pattern. By modulating the time-delay of the retransmitted signal of the PARC, the polarimetric radar is calibrated with the DPC method. The simulations verify that the single dual-polarized antenna DPC scheme possesses better calibration accuracy than the double-antenna DPC scheme.

articleTitle: An improved method for SAR image coastline detection based on despeckling and SVM
abstract: Coastline detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image is an important component for SAR image interpretation. However, because of speckling, SAR image coastline detection with high accuracy is far from resolved. In the paper, an improved method using multiscale wavelet-based despeckling and support vector machine (SVM) based classification is proposed for SAR image coastline detection. In the method, as a pre-process step, a multi-scale wavelet SAR image despeckling strategy is proposed to suppress the noise of SAR image. Base on despeckled SAR image, a novel method for water and non-water classification using circular-window Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and SVM is proposed. GLCM of circular-window is designed as texture feature of water and non-water areas for classification. Feature vector of eighteen dimensions is derived from GLCM and fed into a SVM-based classifier to get water region, the contour of water region is extracted as coastline. The experimental results using real SAR images demonstrate that the proposed approach has better performance compared with other ones.

articleTitle: Analysis of parallel performance of MPI based parallel FDTD on supercomputer
abstract: With the development of multi-core processors, computer clusters and the application of parallel MPI technique, the study of electromagnetic fields numerical arithmetic can improve the capacity of solving large problems. In this paper, based on the platform from National Supercomputing Center in Tianjin (NSCC-TJ: Ranked first in the world in 2010.11), some tests about the parallel efficiency of the parallel FDTD code are made to provide a general rule for a best performance of FDTD on multi-core computers. The results show that following this rule, we can achieve the highest computational efficiency on a more advanced platform.

articleTitle: A disposition algorithm for radar netting
abstract: Netted radar systems are known for being able to achieve better radar performance by fusing information obtained from multiple radars. An effective radar disposition algorithm is proposed in this paper. The mathematical model for radar optimal disposition is established according to the coverage diagrams of radars, RCS of the interested targets, bandwidth, signal pattern differences, etc. The optimal disposition is computed by an ant colony algorithm successfully. Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm performs well in radar netting.

articleTitle: Characterization of level sea-ice thickness in the labrador sea using C-band polarimetric SAR data
abstract: In this paper, we investigated the correlation between sea-ice thickness and SAR polarimetric scattering characteristics using four quad-polarimetric RADARSAT-2 SAR images and sea-ice thickness data provided by helicopter-borne electromagnetic instrument (HEM) in the Labrador Sea. It is shown that co-polarized ratio, entropy and alpha angle are sensitive to sea-ice thickness which would provide a reference for the subsequent research on sea-ice thickness retrieval by SAR data. In this paper, co-polarized ratio proposed mainly by recent research had been tried to retrieve sea-ice thickness, then the error was calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: RCS analysis of general uniaxial media using equivalence principle algorithm
abstract: In this paper, the equivalence principle algorithm (EPA) is proposed to solve electromagnetic scattering from periodic arrays of general uniaxial media. The equivalence principle allows the replacement of unknown electric and magnetic currents on the uniaxial media by equivalence electric and magnetic currents residing on the surface that bounds the uniaxial media. With the EPA, the number of unknowns and memory requirement could be decreased. In this manner, calculations of complicate Green's function for the uniaxial media can be greatly reduced. Numerical results demonstrate that computational time and memory requirement are decreased while solving scattering problem of general uniaxial media arrays.

articleTitle: Optical/SAR image registration based on cross-correlation with multi-scale and multi-direction Gabor characteristic matrixes
abstract: Optical/SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) image registration is one of the key technologies in image fusion or image guidance with SAR imaging. Generally we implement characteristic extraction and scene matching on image registration with optical and SAR images. This paper presents a new heterogeneous optical/SAR image registration method. Firstly we implement directional Frost filtering on SAR image so that we can reduce coherent speckle and keep the details of the edges and textures. Secondly we carry out the Gaussian gradient image of the optical and SAR image respectively. Then we extract characteristics from the two Gaussian gradient images using two-dimensional multi-scale and multi-direction Gabor filters respectively and then form two Gabor characteristic matrixes. Finally we implement NCC (normalized cross-correlation) matching on the two characteristic matrixes. The experiment result shows that the heterogeneous image registration method mentioned in this paper has preferable robustness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Wavelet transform and singular value decomposition based clutter reduction for through wall imaging
abstract: Wavelet transform and singular value decomposition based clutter reduction scheme is proposed for through wall imaging which is capable of discriminating between target, noise and clutter signals. Singular value decomposition is used to reduce clutter and wavelet transform is used to further suppress noise signals (which results in enhancement of target signals). Proposed scheme significantly work well especially for extracting multiple targets in heavy clutters. Selection of different parameters (like mother wavelet, threshold type, threshold parameter, decomposition level and filter order etc) are explored for through wall imaging. Existing and proposed schemes are compared on the basis of mean square error, peak signal to noise ratio and visual inspection.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler of non-ideal scattering centers
abstract: Non-ideal scattering centers exist commonly on radar targets. The scattering characteristics of them induce additional modulation or components to the micro-Doppler. Two typical kinds of non-ideal scattering centers are analyzed and micro-Doppler model of the scattering centers on the ring structure of precession targets are introduced as a detailed example. The experimental results demonstrate the model.

articleTitle: A novel probability-constrained approach to robust wideband beamforming with sensor delay lines
abstract: To improve robustness of the wideband beamformer against look direction error, a low computational complexity robust wideband beamforming algorithm with sensor delay lines (SDLs) is proposed by extending the narrowband robust beamforming method to the wideband case. Based on the SDL wideband model, this wideband beamforming optimizing formula originally consists of a group of probabilistic constraints imposed on the sampled frequency points and the coefficient vector constraint. By constraining the Euclidean distance between the response at reference frequency points and that at others over the angles of interest, these probabilistic constraints can be replaced by just one constraint on the reference frequency point and the computational complexity is reduced. The last optimizing formula can be solved with interior point method after being reformed to the second order cone programming (SOCP). The simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive ground clutter suppression for airborne weather radar based on echoes power
abstract: Airborne weather radar is an important navigation equipment to ensure flight safety.
